docs.title: Stepper-C — Stepper Motor Control in C
docs.text: Quick start

docs.title: A motor running in one file
docs.text:
Two callbacks connect the library to the power stage: one writes the PWM compare values, one switches the gate drivers. The PWM/ADC interrupt passes the raw ADC readings to the fast loop; the main loop runs the slow loop once per millisecond and gives the commands.

#include "sstep.h"

static struct sstep motor;

static int pwm_write(void* context, const uint16_t compare[SSTEP_LEGS_MAX])
{
    (void)context;
    board_pwm_set(compare);
    return 0;
}

static int output_enable(void* context, bool enable)
{
    (void)context;
    board_gates_enable(enable);
    return 0;
}

/* 17HS19-2004S1 on a B-G431B-ESC1: 24 V, 20 kHz PWM, 16 microsteps */
static const struct sstep_config motor_config = {
    .motor = {.r_mohm = 1600U, .l_uh = 3000U, .i_rated_ma = 2000U,
              .ke_uv_s_per_rad = 208600U, .full_steps_per_rev = 200U},
    .stage = {.topology = SSTEP_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG, .vbus_nominal_mv = 24000U,
              .vbus_min_mv = 10000U, .vbus_max_mv = 28000U, .i_full_scale_ma = 4000U,
              .i_trip_ma = 3500U, .pwm_period_ticks = 4250U, .pwm_freq_hz = 20000U,
              .adc_i_zero = 2048U, .adc_i_span = 2047, .adc_vbus_mv_full = 34320U,
              .adc_full = 4095U},
    .ctrl = {.drive_mode = SSTEP_DRIVE_CURRENT, .fast_loop_hz = 20000U,
             .slow_loop_hz = 1000U, .microsteps = 16U, .current_bw_hz = 1000U,
             .i_run_ma = 1500U, .i_hold_ma = 500U, .hold_delay_ms = 500U,
             .v_max = 16000U, .accel = 64000U},
    .hal = {.pwm_write = pwm_write, .output_enable = output_enable},
};

/* PWM/ADC interrupt, 20 kHz */
void ADC1_2_IRQHandler(void);
void ADC1_2_IRQHandler(void)
{
    const struct sstep_sample sample = {board_adc_phase_a(), board_adc_phase_b(),
                                        board_adc_vbus()};
    (void)sstep_fast_loop(&motor, &sample);
}

int main(void)
{
    board_init();
    if ((sstep_init(&motor, &motor_config) != SSTEP_OK) || (sstep_enable(&motor) != SSTEP_OK))
    {
        for (;;)
        {
        }
    }
    (void)sstep_move_to(&motor, 3200); /* one revolution */
    for (;;)
    {
        if (board_tick_1ms())
        {
            (void)sstep_slow_loop(&motor);
        }
    }
}

The board_… functions stand for your timer, ADC and GPIO code; the ADC scaling values above must be measured on your board (Configuration).

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
This chapter documents every public function, type and macro of Stepper-C. Include one header; it declares every function and includes the public type headers:

#include "sstep.h"
Header Contents sstep.h All public functions; library version; includes the headers below sstep_config.h Build-time configuration sstep_defs.h Status codes, topologies, fault flags, driver states sstep_ctrl.h Configuration, callbacks, measurements, status, driver instance

Everything else (src/) is private and not installed with the library.

docs.title: Version — sstep.h
docs.text: Macro Value Meaning SSTEP_VERSION_MAJOR, …_MINOR, …_PATCH 1, 1, 0 Version numbers; set by CMake from the latest vX.Y.Z tag, these are the fallbacks SSTEP_VERSION "1.1.0" Version string

docs.title: Configuration — sstep_config.h
docs.text:
Macro Default Meaning SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FIXED, SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FLOAT 0, 1 Values of SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FIXED Numeric backend SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE 1 Compile the full-bridge topology SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG 1 Compile the shared-leg topology SSTEP_CFG_MICROSTEPS_MAX 256U Largest microstep division SSTEP_CFG_SINE_TABLE_BITS 8U Size of the sine table SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS 1 NULL checks in sstep_fast_loop()

Ranges and override rules: Configuration.

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text: Macro Value Meaning SSTEP_OK 0 Success SSTEP_ERR_PARAM -1 NULL pointer or a value outside its documented range SSTEP_ERR_CONFIG -2 Configuration consistent field by field but not as a whole SSTEP_ERR_STATE -3 Call not allowed in the current state SSTEP_ERR_UNSUPPORTED -4 Topology not compiled in

docs.title: Topologies
docs.text:
Value Legs Meaning SSTEP_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE (0) 4 Two H-bridges: phase A between legs 0 and 1, phase B between legs 2 and 3 SSTEP_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG (1) 3 Three half-bridges: phase A between legs 0 and 2, phase B between legs 1 and 2

SSTEP_LEGS_MAX (4U) is the length of the compare array of pwm_write().

docs.title: Fault flags
docs.text: Macro Value Raised when SSTEP_FAULT_NONE 0x0000U No fault SSTEP_FAULT_OVERCURRENT 0x0001U A phase current above i_trip_ma (current drive) SSTEP_FAULT_OVERVOLTAGE 0x0002U Bus voltage above vbus_max_mv SSTEP_FAULT_UNDERVOLTAGE 0x0004U Bus voltage below vbus_min_mv SSTEP_FAULT_HAL 0x0008U A callback returned an error SSTEP_FAULT_EXTERNAL 0x0010U Reported by the application with sstep_report_fault() SSTEP_FAULT_STALL 0x0020U The rotor does not follow the commanded angle (stall detection, stall_time_ms > 0); since 1.1.0. Also together with SSTEP_FAULT_OVERCURRENT when the trip comes while the detector is counting

docs.title: Driver states — enum sstep_state
docs.text: Value Meaning SSTEP_STATE_DISABLED (0) Outputs off SSTEP_STATE_HOLDING (1) Outputs on, position held SSTEP_STATE_MOVING (2) A move or a velocity command is executing SSTEP_STATE_FAULT (3) Outputs off after a fault; leave with sstep_clear_faults()

docs.title: Callbacks
docs.text:
Type Signature Called from sstep_pwm_write_fn int (*)(void* context, const uint16_t compare[SSTEP_LEGS_MAX]) sstep_fast_loop() sstep_output_enable_fn int (*)(void* context, bool enable) Enable, disable and fault paths sstep_fault_fn void (*)(void* context, uint16_t faults) The context that detects a fault sstep_event_fn void (*)(void* context, enum sstep_event event) sstep_slow_loop()

pwm_write and output_enable return 0 on success and a negative value on error (SSTEP_FAULT_HAL). Events (enum sstep_event): SSTEP_EVENT_MOVE_DONE (0, target reached with zero velocity), SSTEP_EVENT_HOLD_CURRENT (1, current reduced at standstill).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Type Members struct sstep_config motor, stage, ctrl, hal struct sstep_motor_cfg r_mohm, l_uh, i_rated_ma, ke_uv_s_per_rad, full_steps_per_rev struct sstep_stage_cfg topology, vbus_nominal_mv, vbus_min_mv, vbus_max_mv, i_full_scale_ma, i_trip_ma, pwm_period_ticks, pwm_freq_hz, dead_time_ns, adc_i_zero, adc_i_span, adc_vbus_mv_full, adc_full struct sstep_ctrl_cfg drive_mode, fast_loop_hz, slow_loop_hz, microsteps, current_bw_hz, i_run_ma, i_hold_ma, hold_delay_ms, v_max, accel, decel, stall_time_ms, stall_filter_us, stall_speed, stall_sync_pct (since 1.1.0) struct sstep_callbacks context, pwm_write, output_enable, on_fault, on_event enum sstep_drive_mode SSTEP_DRIVE_CURRENT (0), SSTEP_DRIVE_VOLTAGE (1)

Units, ranges and examples of every member: Run-time configuration.

docs.title: Measurement and status
docs.text:
Type Member Unit struct sstep_sample i_a, i_b Phase currents, ADC counts (ignored in voltage drive) vbus Bus voltage, ADC counts struct sstep_status state, faults enum sstep_state, fault flags position, target microsteps velocity microsteps/s (commanded) i_a_ma, i_b_ma mA (last measured) vbus_mv mV (last measured) emf_d_mv, emf_q_mv mV, filtered back-EMF estimate along and 90° ahead of the commanded current (since 1.1.0) rotor_velocity microsteps/s, estimated from the back-EMF (since 1.1.0) load_angle_cdeg 0.01°, estimated load angle, commanded minus rotor electrical angle (since 1.1.0) stall_level_pct %, stall detector level, 100 = trip (since 1.1.0)

The five estimates are 0 while stall detection is off; their equations are in Stall detection.

docs.title: Driver instance
docs.text: struct sstep is an opaque array of SSTEP_INSTANCE_WORDS 64-bit words (on Cortex-M4 432 B fixed point, 456 B float; on 64-bit hosts 456 B and 480 B). Allocate it, pass its address, never read or write its content. SSTEP_CONFIG_BYTES is the size of the configuration copy (152 B with 32-bit pointers, 176 B with 64-bit pointers) and SSTEP_STATE_BYTES the size of the private state behind it.

docs.title: Functions — sstep.h
docs.text: All functions return a status code. Positions are in microsteps, velocities in microsteps/s, currents in mA. Every function except sstep_init() returns SSTEP_ERR_STATE for an instance without a successful sstep_init() and then calls no callback (sstep_fast_loop() only with SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS = 1); the tables below list the other cases.

docs.title: sstep_init
docs.text:
int sstep_init(struct sstep* drv, const struct sstep_config* cfg);

Validate a configuration and initialize a driver; the outputs stay off. Derives the per-unit bases, the PI gains (\(K_p = L\,\omega_c\), \(K_i = R\,\omega_c\)), the trajectory constants and, with stall_time_ms > 0, the stall detector constants without floating point. Calls no callback.

Parameter Description drv Driver instance cfg Configuration; copied Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Success, state SSTEP_STATE_DISABLED SSTEP_ERR_PARAM NULL pointer, missing required callback or a field out of range SSTEP_ERR_CONFIG Inconsistent fields (for example i_run_ma > i_trip_ma, stall detection with voltage drive or without ke_uv_s_per_rad) or a gain that does not fit SSTEP_ERR_UNSUPPORTED Topology not compiled in

docs.title: sstep_enable
docs.text:
int sstep_enable(struct sstep* drv);

Switch the outputs on and hold the current position with the run current; resets the current controllers. Does nothing when already enabled.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Enabled (SSTEP_STATE_HOLDING) SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL SSTEP_ERR_STATE Faulted, or output_enable() failed (then SSTEP_FAULT_HAL)

docs.title: sstep_disable
docs.text:
int sstep_disable(struct sstep* drv);

Switch the outputs off at once (the motor coasts, no holding torque) and cancel the command. A faulted driver stays faulted.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Disabled SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL

docs.title: sstep_fast_loop
docs.text:
int sstep_fast_loop(struct sstep* drv, const struct sstep_sample* sample);

Convert the measurements, check the trip levels, run the current controllers, limit the voltage, compute the leg duty cycles and call pwm_write(). Call from the PWM/ADC interrupt at fast_loop_hz. The measurements are stored in every state; control and protection run only while the outputs are on.

Parameter Description drv Driver instance sample Raw ADC readings of this period Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Done (faults are reported through the state and on_fault()) SSTEP_ERR_PARAM NULL argument; only with SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS = 1

docs.title: sstep_slow_loop
docs.text:
int sstep_slow_loop(struct sstep* drv);

Advance the trajectory by one period, prepare the setpoint of the fast loop, switch between run and hold current, compensate the bus voltage, update the state and report events. Call at slow_loop_hz.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Done SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL

docs.title: sstep_move_to
docs.text:
int sstep_move_to(struct sstep* drv, int32_t position);

Move to an absolute position with the trapezoidal profile. Replaces the running command without a velocity step.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Accepted SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL SSTEP_ERR_STATE Disabled or faulted

docs.title: sstep_move_by
docs.text:
int sstep_move_by(struct sstep* drv, int32_t delta);

Move by delta relative to the current target.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Accepted SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL, or the new target is outside int32_t SSTEP_ERR_STATE Disabled or faulted

docs.title: sstep_run
docs.text:
int sstep_run(struct sstep* drv, int32_t velocity);

Accelerate or decelerate to a signed constant velocity and keep it until another command.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Accepted SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL, or |velocity| > v_max SSTEP_ERR_STATE Disabled or faulted

docs.title: sstep_stop
docs.text:
int sstep_stop(struct sstep* drv);

Decelerate to standstill with the configured deceleration and hold there. Does nothing when the motor is not moving.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Accepted or nothing to stop SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL

docs.title: sstep_set_position
docs.text:
int sstep_set_position(struct sstep* drv, int32_t position);

Give the current position a new value (homing). The electrical angle is kept, so the rotor does not move.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Done SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL SSTEP_ERR_STATE A command is executing

docs.title: sstep_set_current
docs.text:
int sstep_set_current(struct sstep* drv, uint32_t run_ma, uint32_t hold_ma);

Change the run and hold currents; used from the next slow period.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Done SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL, run_ma is 0 or a value above \(10^7\) SSTEP_ERR_CONFIG hold_ma > run_ma, or run_ma above i_trip_ma or i_rated_ma

docs.title: sstep_set_motion_limits
docs.text:
int sstep_set_motion_limits(struct sstep* drv, uint32_t v_max, uint32_t accel, uint32_t decel);

Change the velocity limit, the acceleration and the deceleration (decel = 0: same as accel). They apply from the next slow period, also to a running command.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Done SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL, or a value that rounds to zero or is too large (ranges)

docs.title: sstep_report_fault
docs.text:
int sstep_report_fault(struct sstep* drv, uint16_t faults);

Raise fault flags detected by the application (gate driver fault pin, temperature): the outputs go off at once and on_fault() is called. May be called from an interrupt. SSTEP_FAULT_NONE does nothing.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Done SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL

docs.title: sstep_clear_faults
docs.text:
int sstep_clear_faults(struct sstep* drv);

Clear all fault flags; the driver goes to SSTEP_STATE_DISABLED and can be enabled again.

Return Meaning SSTEP_OK Done SSTEP_ERR_PARAM drv is NULL

docs.title: sstep_get_status
docs.text:
int sstep_get_status(const struct sstep* drv, struct sstep_status* status);

Read a snapshot of the state, faults, commanded motion, the last measurements and the stall detector estimates in engineering units. With stall detection on it also converts the back-EMF estimate (a square root and a CORDIC arctangent, about 1200 instructions on Cortex-M4): call it from the slow-loop context, not from the fast loop.

Parameter Description drv Driver instance status Filled on success Return Meaning SSTEP_OK status filled SSTEP_ERR_PARAM A NULL pointer

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: This chapter explains how Stepper-C is built: its modules, the two loops and how they exchange data, the driver states, the memory model, error handling and the rules for calling it from interrupts. The control algorithms themselves (current control, microstepping, trajectory, voltage limits) are described in Motor Control.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Module Files Responsibility Public API sstep.h, inc/sstep_ctrl.h, inc/sstep_defs.h, inc/sstep_config.h Functions, configuration and status types, status codes, fault flags, build-time options Control src/sstep_ctrl.c Configuration check, derived constants, fast loop (current control, protection, PWM), slow loop (setpoints, hold current, events), commands, state machine Stall detection src/sstep_stall.c Back-EMF observer (fast loop), stall decision (slow loop), estimates of the status Motion src/sstep_motion.c Trapezoidal trajectory in integer arithmetic (both backends) Power stage src/sstep_bridge.c Voltage limit of the topology, phase voltages to leg compare values Numeric backend src/sstep_math.h, src/sstep_math.c, src/sstep_sin_table.c Saturating Q15/Q31 or float operations, gains, sine/cosine table

Only the public API is visible to the application. Everything under src/ is private: the driver instance struct sstep is an opaque block of memory whose layout may change in any release.

docs.title: The two loops
docs.text:
The application calls two functions periodically. Both work on the same instance.

Fast loop sstep_fast_loop() Slow loop sstep_slow_loop() Rate fast_loop_hz, typically the PWM frequency (20 kHz) slow_loop_hz, typically 1 kHz; fast_loop_hz must be an integer multiple Context PWM/ADC interrupt Main loop or a timer task Input Raw ADC counts: phase A and B currents, bus voltage Commands given since the last call Work Convert the measurements, check the trip levels, interpolate the electrical angle, current references, PI controllers, voltage limit, leg duty cycles; back-EMF observer (stall detection) Advance the trajectory one step, compute the setpoint of the next slow period, hold current, bus voltage compensation, state, events, stall decision Output pwm_write() with one compare value per leg A setpoint for the fast loop; on_event() Time Bounded: no loops over data; the only loops have fixed limits (voltage pre-scale at most 18, division at most 16 iterations); two divisions, only while the voltage is limited Bounded: integer square root at most 32 iterations; one gain computation for the bus voltage

Hand-off. The slow loop computes a setpoint for the next slow period: the electrical angle at its start, the angle increment per fast period, the current amplitude, the back-EMF feed-forward and the bus voltage correction. It writes it into the free half of a double buffer and marks it pending. The fast loop takes a pending setpoint at the start of its next period and from then on advances the angle by the increment once per period. If the slow loop is late, the fast loop stops advancing after fast_loop_hz / slow_loop_hz periods and holds the angle, so a late slow loop never makes the motor run ahead of the trajectory.

The fast loop never reads the half being written: sp_pending is cleared before the write and set after it. This relies on the fast loop interrupting the slow loop on the same core, never running in parallel with it.

docs.title: Driver states
docs.text:
State Outputs Entered by Left by SSTEP_STATE_DISABLED Off (all legs high impedance) sstep_init(), sstep_disable(), sstep_clear_faults() sstep_enable() SSTEP_STATE_HOLDING On, holding the position sstep_enable(); a move or stop completes A command; a fault; sstep_disable() SSTEP_STATE_MOVING On, following the trajectory sstep_move_to(), sstep_move_by(), sstep_run() (seen at the next slow loop) Move or stop completes; a fault; sstep_disable() SSTEP_STATE_FAULT Off Any fault, in any active state sstep_clear_faults() only

The state is updated by the slow loop; a command changes it at the next sstep_slow_loop(). Faults switch the outputs off immediately, in the context that detects them.

docs.title: Memory model
docs.text:
Object Owner Size Lifetime struct sstep (driver instance) Application (static, stack or pool) 432 B fixed point, 456 B float on Cortex-M4 From sstep_init() as long as the motor runs struct sstep_config Application; copied by sstep_init() 152 B on Cortex-M4 Only during sstep_init() struct sstep_sample Application 6 B Only during sstep_fast_loop() struct sstep_status Application 48 B on Cortex-M4 Filled by sstep_get_status() Sine table Library, static const (flash) 514 B fixed point, 1028 B float (default 257 entries) Program

There is no heap, no global or static mutable variable and no hidden buffer: everything the library writes is in the instance or in the caller's structures. Several instances (axes) are independent.

The instance size is fixed at compile time by SSTEP_INSTANCE_WORDS in sstep_ctrl.h (from SSTEP_CONFIG_BYTES and SSTEP_STATE_BYTES, plain constants so that static analysis can evaluate them) and checked against the private state by _Static_assert.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Situation Result NULL instance, configuration or sample SSTEP_ERR_PARAM; nothing is changed A configuration field outside its range or a missing required callback sstep_init() returns SSTEP_ERR_PARAM Fields that are valid alone but not together (trip above full scale, bandwidth above fast_loop_hz / 4, a gain that does not fit) sstep_init() returns SSTEP_ERR_CONFIG A topology that is not compiled in sstep_init() returns SSTEP_ERR_UNSUPPORTED Any call before a successful sstep_init() (zeroed instance, or the last sstep_init() failed in the derivation) SSTEP_ERR_STATE; no callback is called A motion command while disabled or faulted SSTEP_ERR_STATE A phase current above i_trip_ma (current drive) SSTEP_FAULT_OVERCURRENT, outputs off in the same fast period Bus voltage above vbus_max_mv or below vbus_min_mv SSTEP_FAULT_OVERVOLTAGE / SSTEP_FAULT_UNDERVOLTAGE, outputs off pwm_write() or output_enable() returns a negative value SSTEP_FAULT_HAL, outputs off The rotor does not follow the commanded angle for stall_time_ms (stall detection on) SSTEP_FAULT_STALL, outputs off in the slow loop sstep_report_fault() The given flags, outputs off

Every fault calls output_enable(false) and then on_fault() (if set) with the new flags, in the context that detected it. Faults accumulate until sstep_clear_faults(). Arithmetic never overflows: every operation of the numeric backend saturates.

docs.title: Threading and reentrancy
docs.text:
• Per instance, two contexts: sstep_fast_loop() from the PWM/ADC interrupt; every other function from one task or the main loop (the slow-loop context).
  • sstep_report_fault() may also be called from an interrupt.
  • No locking inside. The hand-off between the loops is lock-free on a single core (see above). Do not call the slow-loop functions from two tasks without your own mutex.
  • Multi-core: both loops of one instance must run on the same core.
  • Different instances share nothing and may run on different cores.
  • Callbacks run in the context of the function that calls them: pwm_write() and on_fault() may run in the interrupt.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Decision Reason Two loops at different rates Current control needs the PWM rate; the trajectory and the square root of the motion planner do not. The fast loop stays short and bounded. Configuration in integer engineering units Values from the datasheet and the schematic are entered as they are (r_mohm = 1600); no floating point is needed to configure a fixed-point build. Gains derived by the library Kp and Ki follow from R, L and one bandwidth value; there is nothing to tune by hand for a first run. Fixed point and float backends with the same ranges The same code and the same tests run on MCUs with and without FPU; the results match within the quantization. Motion planner in integer arithmetic in both backends Positions must be exact over long runs; Q16 microsteps in 64 bits never drift. Callbacks given once at initialization No link-time coupling to a HAL; several instances can drive different timers. Raw ADC counts as input The library owns the scaling (zero offset, span, polarity) and the trip levels in counts, so the protection does not depend on a conversion done elsewhere. Opaque instance The application cannot depend on internal fields; the layout can change without breaking the API (MISRA deviation DEV-01).

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Stall detection missed a slipping rotor at low speed. The back-EMF vector of a slipping rotor turns in the commanded frame and stayed above stall_sync_pct about half of the time, so the up/down counter did not accumulate: a heavy axis (load inertia ×100) lost hundreds of full steps without a fault. A reversed back-EMF now keeps the condition true for half of the trip time: SSTEP_FAULT_STALL 43 to 60 ms after the load angle passes 90°.
  • False stall under a heavy load. The inductance error adds to \(\cos\delta\) (it does not scale it, as the documentation said), so a synchronous rotor at 72 % of the pull-out torque with \(R\) +30 %, \(L\) −20 % tripped. The condition in motion now also requires the d axis inside the window of a rotor that does not turn. The same window removes the false trip at the voltage limit: 11 rev/s at 24 V now runs with the example stall_sync_pct of 50.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• SSTEP_FAULT_OVERCURRENT comes together with SSTEP_FAULT_STALL when the trip finds the stall detector counting: a light rotor reaches the trip before stall_time_ms, and the position is lost. An application that compares faults with a single flag must test the bits. Without stall detection nothing changes.
  • A load angle swinging repeatedly beyond about 120° near the voltage limit is reported as a stall even before a step is lost (documented in Limits).
  • SSTEP_STATE_BYTES on 64-bit hosts: 288 B fixed point, 312 B float (Cortex-M4 unchanged: 280 B, 304 B). Flash on Cortex-M4 (-Os): 9216 B fixed point, 9894 B float. Worst-case stack of sstep_slow_loop() 152 B fixed point (float 140 B); the slow loop executes about 145 more instructions per period with stall detection on (-Os); the fast loop is unchanged.

Sensorless stall detection. Compatible with 1.0.0: the new configuration fields are zero in existing initializers, which keeps stall detection off and the behaviour unchanged; rebuild the application with the new headers (the instance size changed).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Stall detection (src/sstep_stall.c): a back-EMF observer in the fast loop (e = v − R·i − L·di/dt from the applied voltage, the measured currents and the commanded angle, filtered in the commanded current frame) and a decision in the slow loop. In motion it checks that the back-EMF along the commanded motion stays above stall_sync_pct of Ke·ω; at rest and at low speed it checks that the rotor does not turn faster than the command by more than stall_speed, with the observer offset (resistance, dead time) learned while the rotor follows. An up/down counter raises the new fault SSTEP_FAULT_STALL (0x0020U) after stall_time_ms, with the usual fault behaviour (outputs off, SSTEP_STATE_FAULT, on_fault(), cleared by sstep_clear_faults()).
  • Configuration (struct sstep_ctrl_cfg): stall_time_ms (0 = off, the default), stall_filter_us, stall_speed, stall_sync_pct. sstep_init() returns SSTEP_ERR_CONFIG for stall detection with voltage drive or without ke_uv_s_per_rad.
  • Status (struct sstep_status): emf_d_mv, emf_q_mv, rotor_velocity, load_angle_cdeg, stall_level_pct.
  • Documentation: the stall detection section of Motor Control (principle, the exact equations for a model, design decisions, parameter choice, measured results, cost, limits), configuration, usage, integration and API updates. New hero illustrations (docs/assets/images/hero-dark.png for the website and the PDF cover, hero-light.png for the README).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• struct sstep grows by 96 B (432 B fixed point, 456 B float on Cortex-M4): SSTEP_CONFIG_BYTES 152 / 176 B, SSTEP_STATE_BYTES 280 / 304 B. struct sstep_status grows from 32 B to 48 B.
  • Flash on Cortex-M4 (-Os): 9040 B fixed point, 9718 B float. Worst-case stack of sstep_fast_loop() 216 B fixed point (128 B float), of sstep_get_status() 92 B.
  • With stall detection on, the fast loop executes about 240 more instructions per period (-O2, both backends; 475 fixed point and 213 float with -Os).

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
• 93 GoogleTest tests (fixed point) and 92 (float), 100 % line, branch and function coverage of src/ in both backends. The motor model of the tests gained a detent torque, a dead-time voltage error, a configurable current quantization and an imposed rotor motion for synthetic tests.
  • Stall detection on the motor model: the reference case (17HS19-2004S1, three-leg stage, 24 V, 0.12 N·m held at 1.5 A but not at the 0.5 A hold current) reports SSTEP_FAULT_STALL 48 ms after the load angle passes 90°; a hard stop at 3 rev/s after 50 ms. No fault through enable, run → hold, moves, reversal and runs from 0.125 to 11 rev/s, also with R +30 %, L −20 %, 70 mV dead time per leg, 29 mA current quantization and detent torque (largest detector level 32 %).
  • MISRA C:2012: 0 violations, no new deviation.
First release: closed-loop microstepping current control for two-phase hybrid stepper motors in portable C11.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Public API (sstep.h, 15 functions): sstep_init(), sstep_enable(), sstep_disable(), sstep_fast_loop(), sstep_slow_loop(), sstep_move_to(), sstep_move_by(), sstep_run(), sstep_stop(), sstep_set_position(), sstep_set_current(), sstep_set_motion_limits(), sstep_report_fault(), sstep_clear_faults(), sstep_get_status().
  • Types (inc/sstep_ctrl.h, inc/sstep_defs.h): configuration in integer engineering units (motor, power stage and measurement, control and motion), hardware callbacks given at initialization (pwm_write, output_enable, optional on_fault, on_event), raw ADC sample, status in engineering units, status codes, fault flags, driver states. pwm_freq_hz and dead_time_ns are reserved for later versions.
  • Opaque driver instance: struct sstep is uint64_t opaque[SSTEP_INSTANCE_WORDS], allocated by the application (336 B fixed point, 360 B float on Cortex-M4); the driver state and every numeric type stay private in src/.
  • Current control: PI controller per phase with gains derived from R, L and the bandwidth (Kp = L wc, Ki = R wc), back-EMF feed-forward, back-calculation anti-windup, bus voltage compensation; open-loop voltage drive for boards without current sensing.
  • Microstepping: 1 to 256 microsteps per full step, 32-bit electrical angle, quarter-wave sine table with linear interpolation (generated by tools/sstep_gen_sin_table.py), angle interpolated at the fast-loop rate.
  • Motion planner: trapezoidal moves without overshoot in integer arithmetic (positions in 1/65536 microstep, 64 bits), separate acceleration and deceleration, smooth retargeting, constant-velocity runs, stop, homing with sstep_set_position(), hold current after a standstill delay, SSTEP_EVENT_MOVE_DONE and SSTEP_EVENT_HOLD_CURRENT.
  • Power stages: two H-bridges (4 legs) and three half-bridges with a shared leg (3 legs); the voltage request is limited to the topology with its direction kept.
  • Protection: overcurrent, overvoltage and undervoltage trips in the fast loop, callback errors and external faults switch the outputs off in the same period. Every function except sstep_init() returns SSTEP_ERR_STATE for an instance that was not initialized successfully, without touching the hardware.
  • Numeric backends: fixed point (Q15/Q31, integer only) and single-precision float, selected with SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND (CMake) or SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND.
  • Build-time options (inc/sstep_config.h, overridable in sstep_user_config.h): topologies, largest microstep division, sine table size, argument checks of the fast loop.
  • Build: CMake library target in sstep.cmake, presets for Debug, Release and the unit tests of both backends; misra-analyze, cppcheck-analyze and codeql-analyze targets.
  • Documentation: website and PDF manual: introduction, getting started, architecture, usage, extending, configuration with the measured stack and memory footprint, motor control theory with measured results, integration guide, API reference, MISRA compliance.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
• 78 GoogleTest tests (fixed point) and 77 (float): numeric backend, power stage, motion planner, API and closed loop on a motor model (tests/unit/sstep_test_plant.hpp); 100 % line, branch and function coverage of src/ in both backends.
  • Closed loop on the motor model (17HS19-2004S1, 24 V, 20 kHz, 1 kHz bandwidth), matching the Scilab prototype: current step overshoot 1.11 %, settling 0.40 ms; 8 rev/s current 1.862 A with two H-bridges and 1.557 A with a shared leg; load angle at 0.25 N·m 37.21°.
  • MISRA C:2012: 0 violations (Cppcheck 2.13 and 2.16), one documented deviation (DEV-01, Rule 11.3, opaque instance).
  • No warnings with -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion (GCC on x86-64 and arm-none-eabi-gcc for Cortex-M4); clean under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.
  • Cortex-M4 (GCC 15.2, -Os): 6980 B flash fixed point, 7446 B float; worst-case stack of sstep_fast_loop() 184 B / 128 B; .data and .bss empty.
  • Sine table error (default 8 bits): 1.0 LSB of Q15 (fixed point), 4.8·10^-6 (float).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Stepper-C has two kinds of configuration. Build-time options select the code that is compiled in (numeric backend, topologies, table size); they are macros in inc/sstep_config.h. Run-time configuration describes the motor, the power stage and the control; it is a struct sstep_config passed to sstep_init(). This chapter lists both, then the memory footprint and the measured stack usage.

docs.title: Build-time options
docs.text:
Each macro has a default, is range-checked with #error and can be overridden on the compiler command line or in a header sstep_user_config.h (included when SSTEP_USER_CONFIG is defined; with CMake, set SSTEP_CONFIG_DIR to its folder). The application must be compiled with the same values as the library: they change the size of struct sstep.

Macro Default Range Meaning SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FIXED …_FIXED, …_FLOAT Numeric backend (CMake: SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND=FIXED or FLOAT) SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE 1 0, 1 Compile the two-H-bridge topology SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG 1 0, 1 Compile the three-leg topology; at least one must be 1 SSTEP_CFG_MICROSTEPS_MAX 256U power of two, 1 .. 256 Largest microsteps accepted by sstep_init() SSTEP_CFG_SINE_TABLE_BITS 8U 6 .. 10 Quarter-wave table of \(2^\mathrm{bits} + 1\) entries (see the accuracy table) SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS 1 0, 1 0 removes the NULL checks from sstep_fast_loop() only

docs.title: Run-time configuration
docs.text: struct sstep_config has four parts. All values are integers in engineering units; sstep_init() copies the structure, so it may be a temporary or a const in flash. Fields outside their range make sstep_init() return SSTEP_ERR_PARAM; combinations that do not fit return SSTEP_ERR_CONFIG.

docs.title: Callbacks
docs.text: Field Required Called from Contract context – – Passed unchanged to every callback pwm_write Yes sstep_fast_loop() Load one compare value per leg (compare[0..3], compare[3] is 0 for the shared leg) for the next PWM period; return 0, or a negative value on error output_enable Yes Any function that enables, disables or faults true: enable the gate drivers; false: all legs high impedance. Return 0, or a negative value on error on_fault No The context that detects the fault (may be the interrupt) Informs the application of new fault flags; outputs are already off on_event No sstep_slow_loop() SSTEP_EVENT_MOVE_DONE, SSTEP_EVENT_HOLD_CURRENT

docs.title: Memory footprint
docs.text:
Measured with arm-none-eabi-gcc 15.2.1 for Cortex-M4 (-mthumb, float backend with -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16 -mfloat-abi=hard), default build-time options, both topologies.

Object Fixed point Float struct sstep (RAM per motor) 432 B 456 B Code and constants, -Os (flash) 9216 B 9894 B of which the sine table 514 B 1028 B .data + .bss 0 B 0 B

struct sstep is the configuration copy (SSTEP_CONFIG_BYTES: 152 B on Cortex-M4, 176 B on 64-bit hosts) plus the private state (SSTEP_STATE_BYTES: 280 B fixed point, 304 B float on Cortex-M4; 288 B and 312 B on 64-bit hosts); on a 64-bit host the instance is 464 B and 488 B. Stall detection accounts for 96 B of it on Cortex-M4, and for 2236 B (fixed point) or 2448 B (float) of the flash whether it is enabled or not.

docs.title: Stack usage
docs.text:
Worst-case stack of each public function including the library functions it calls, measured with -fstack-usage -fcallgraph-info=su and tools/docs/stack_usage.py (Cortex-M4, toolchain as above). Calls through the callbacks are not included: add the stack of your pwm_write(), output_enable(), on_fault() and on_event() to the functions that call them.

Function Fixed -Os Fixed -O0 Float -Os Float -O0 sstep_init() 224 1544 200 1432 sstep_enable() 48 80 64 88 sstep_disable() 24 40 24 40 sstep_fast_loop() 216 304 128 312 sstep_slow_loop() 152 696 140 624 sstep_move_to() 0 48 0 48 sstep_move_by() 0 112 0 112 sstep_run() 16 104 16 104 sstep_stop() 0 40 0 40 sstep_set_position() 16 72 16 72 sstep_set_current() 52 216 36 128 sstep_set_motion_limits() 72 224 72 224 sstep_report_fault() 24 40 24 40 sstep_clear_faults() 0 40 0 40 sstep_get_status() 92 536 92 496

The interrupt stack must hold the frame of sstep_fast_loop() plus pwm_write() (and output_enable() + on_fault() for the fault path) plus the interrupt entry. There is no recursion; every frame is static.

To re-measure:

mkdir stack && cd stack
arm-none-eabi-gcc -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -Os -std=c11 -fstack-usage -fcallgraph-info=su \
    -I.. -I../inc -c ../src/*.c
python ../tools/docs/stack_usage.py . --markdown

docs.title: Extending the Library
docs.text: Most extensions are built on top of Stepper-C without changing it: homing, limit switches, communication, multi-axis coordination and encoders are application code that calls the public API. This chapter shows where each extension belongs and the rules for changes to the library itself.

docs.title: Where to extend
docs.text: You want to… Do it in Library change needed? Drive another MCU or board Your pwm_write(), output_enable(), ADC and interrupt code No Home the axis on a switch Application: sstep_run() towards the switch, sstep_stop() on the edge, sstep_set_position(0) No Add soft limits Application: clamp targets before sstep_move_to() No Accept commands over UART, CAN, Modbus Application: protocol handler that calls the commands from the slow-loop context No Coordinate several axes Application: one instance per axis, start moves in the same slow period, scale v_max per axis No Detect a stall without a sensor Configuration: stall_time_ms and the other stall_* fields (Stall detection) No Detect a stall with an encoder Application: compare the encoder with sstep_get_status() position, sstep_report_fault() on a large difference No Report a temperature or driver fault sstep_report_fault() from the interrupt or task that detects it No Use another numeric format or table size Build-time options in sstep_user_config.h No Support a new power stage topology src/sstep_bridge.c (limit and duty cycles), enum sstep_topology, a build-time option Yes A different motion profile (S-curve) src/sstep_motion.c Yes Dead-time compensation Fast loop; the configuration already has dead_time_ns Yes

docs.title: Homing example
docs.text:
enum homing_state { HOMING_SEEK, HOMING_STOP, HOMING_DONE };

static enum homing_state homing = HOMING_SEEK;

/* called from the slow-loop context after sstep_slow_loop() */
void homing_step(bool switch_pressed)
{
    struct sstep_status st;
    switch (homing)
    {
    case HOMING_SEEK:
        if (switch_pressed)
        {
            (void)sstep_stop(&motor);
            homing = HOMING_STOP;
        }
        break;
    case HOMING_STOP:
        if ((sstep_get_status(&motor, &st) == SSTEP_OK) && (st.state == SSTEP_STATE_HOLDING))
        {
            (void)sstep_set_position(&motor, 0);
            homing = HOMING_DONE;
        }
        break;
    default:
        break;
    }
}

Start it with sstep_run(&motor, -1600) (towards the switch, at a low speed). The stop uses the configured deceleration, so the zero is where the motor came to rest, a few microsteps after the switch; for a repeatable zero, move back off the switch slowly and take the edge again.

docs.title: Changing the configuration
docs.text:
Build-time options go into sstep_user_config.h in a folder of your project:

/* sstep_user_config.h */
#define SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FLOAT
#define SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE 0U /* only the 3-leg stage of this board */
#define SSTEP_CFG_MICROSTEPS_MAX 64U

and CMake gets -DSSTEP_CONFIG_DIR=<folder>. Run-time values (motor, currents, limits) need no rebuild: pass another struct sstep_config to sstep_init(), or use sstep_set_current() and sstep_set_motion_limits() while running.

docs.title: Contributing to the library
docs.text:
1. Code. C11, no new dependencies, no heap, no global state; the rules of misra-analyze; internal types stay in src/, sstep.h declares the public API only.
  2. Both backends. Every arithmetic change works with fixed point and float; the [UnitTests] and [UnitTestsFloat] presets must both pass.
  3. Tests. 100 % line and branch coverage of src/; a closed-loop test on the motor model for any change of the control behavior.
  4. Instance size. If the private state grows, update SSTEP_STATE_BYTES in inc/sstep_ctrl.h; the build fails until it fits.
  5. Analysis. misra-analyze 0 violations, or a recorded deviation in MISRA C:2012.
  6. Format. clang-format reports no changes in the files you touched.
  7. Documentation. The affected pages, the stack table, the diagrams and CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased].
  8. Compatibility. The public API is stable within a major version.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This chapter shows how to get Stepper-C, add it to your project, and build and test it.

docs.title: Get the library
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/AntonVynohradov/Stepper-C.git

Each release provides the source code, a prebuilt static library for Linux x86-64 with its headers, the MISRA report and the PDF user manual.

docs.title: Add it to your project
docs.text:
CMake.

include(path/to/Stepper-C/sstep.cmake)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE sstep)

Any other build system. Compile src/*.c and add the repository root and inc/ to the include path.

Prebuilt package. Link lib/libsstep.a and add include/ to the include path.

docs.title: Prerequisites for development
docs.text:
• C11 compiler, CMake 3.20+
  • Optional: GoogleTest and gcovr, Python 3, Cppcheck, clang-format, MkDocs (requirements-dev.txt), Doxygen, WeasyPrint with Pango

docs.title: Versioning and releases
docs.text:
Stepper-C follows Semantic Versioning: the public API (sstep.h and inc/) is stable within a major version. The version comes from the latest vX.Y.Z Git tag (cmake/version.cmake), with SSTEP_VERSION in sstep.h as the fallback for builds without CMake; every change is recorded under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md.

A release tag runs release.yml: version check, unit tests with the coverage gate, MISRA gate, release build, and a GitHub Release with the static library, the headers, the MISRA report and the PDF manual.

docs.title: Integration Guide
docs.text:
Stepper-C does not touch hardware. An integration has four parts:

  1. PWM: a timer with one compare channel per leg, loaded by pwm_write().
  2. Measurement: ADC conversions of the two phase currents and the bus voltage, synchronized to the PWM, passed to sstep_fast_loop() as raw counts.
  3. Fast loop interrupt: at the end of each conversion sequence, call sstep_fast_loop().
  4. Slow loop: call sstep_slow_loop() and the commands from one task or the main loop at slow_loop_hz.

docs.title: PWM
docs.text:
• Use center-aligned PWM with the period pwm_period_ticks; one compare value per leg, in the order of the topology: full bridge [A+ A− B+ B−], shared leg [U V W]. A compare value of pwm_period_ticks means the high-side switch is on for the whole period.
  • Load the compare values with preload (shadow registers) so that pwm_write() takes effect at the next period boundary, not in the middle of a period.
  • Dead time is inserted by the timer or the gate driver; the library does not compensate it in this version.
  • output_enable(false) must put every leg in high impedance (for example the timer's main output enable bit and the gate drivers' enable pins), not only set 50 % duty.

docs.title: Current and voltage measurement
docs.text:
• Trigger the ADC from the PWM timer at the center of the period, where the low-side switches conduct and the switching noise is furthest away; with low-side shunts this is the only point where the current is visible.
  • Convert phase A, phase B and the bus voltage in one sequence, and call sstep_fast_loop() from its end-of-conversion interrupt.
  • In the shared-leg topology the two measured currents are the phase currents A and B; the shared leg carries their sum.
  • Measure adc_i_zero with the outputs off after power-up; the library uses the value from the configuration, so re-initialize with the measured value if it differs from the default.

docs.title: Timing
docs.text:
Item Requirement fast_loop_hz The real rate of the end-of-conversion interrupt; usually the PWM frequency or a fraction of it (every second period at 40 kHz PWM) slow_loop_hz The real rate of sstep_slow_loop(); fast_loop_hz must be a multiple of it Jitter of the slow loop Tolerated: the fast loop holds the angle if the slow loop is late, and catches up with the next setpoint Priority The fast-loop interrupt preempts the slow-loop context, never the other way round Execution time of the fast loop Must end well before the next conversion; measure it on your MCU (toggle a pin or read the cycle counter)

The library measures nothing about time: if the configured rates do not match the real ones, the velocities, the accelerations and the hold delay scale accordingly.

docs.title: Bare metal
docs.text:
int main(void)
{
    board_init(); /* clocks, PWM timer, ADC triggered by the timer, interrupts */
    if ((sstep_init(&motor, &motor_config) != SSTEP_OK) || (sstep_enable(&motor) != SSTEP_OK))
    {
        for (;;)
        {
        }
    }
    for (;;)
    {
        if (board_tick_1ms()) /* set by SysTick or a timer */
        {
            (void)sstep_slow_loop(&motor);
            /* commands and the application's state machine here */
        }
    }
}

docs.title: RTOS
docs.text:
Run the slow loop in a periodic task with a fixed period (not a delay after the work), and call every command from that task, or from another task through a queue:

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"

static void motor_task(void* arg)
{
    TickType_t wake = xTaskGetTickCount();
    (void)arg;
    for (;;)
    {
        vTaskDelayUntil(&wake, pdMS_TO_TICKS(1));
        (void)sstep_slow_loop(&motor);
        /* take commands from a queue and call sstep_move_to() etc. here */
    }
}

The fast loop stays in the ADC interrupt; give it a priority above the RTOS kernel's interrupt priority limit only if it calls no RTOS function (the library calls none; check your callbacks).

docs.title: Adding the library to a CMake build
docs.text:
set(SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND FLOAT)                         # MCU with FPU; default FIXED
include(path/to/Stepper-C/sstep.cmake)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE sstep)
target_link_libraries(sstep PUBLIC zephyr_interface)  # Zephyr applications only

The backend and the other build-time options are compile definitions of the sstep target, so the application sees the same values as the library.

Without CMake: compile src/*.c, add the repository root and inc/ to the include path, and pass the same -DSSTEP_CFG_… definitions to the library and the application.

docs.title: Bring-up checklist
docs.text:
1. Outputs off: read the ADC and check adc_i_zero and the bus voltage reading against a multimeter (sstep_get_status() shows vbus_mv after a fast loop).
  2. Polarity: start with drive_mode = SSTEP_DRIVE_VOLTAGE and a small i_run_ma; after sstep_enable(), the measured current of phase A must be positive and close to the reference. If it is negative, negate adc_i_span.
  3. Current loop: switch to SSTEP_DRIVE_CURRENT with a low run current; look at the phase current with a current probe or the status: it must settle at i_run_ma.
  4. Motion: run slowly (sstep_run() with a few hundred microsteps/s), then raise the speed and the acceleration to the application's values.
  5. Protection: check the trips with a lowered i_trip_ma and vbus_max_mv, and the external fault input with sstep_report_fault().
  6. Stall detection (optional): enable it with the example values, log stall_level_pct, emf_d_mv and load_angle_cdeg through every operating point (enable, hold, the fastest move, the heaviest load), then block the shaft by hand at speed and at standstill to see SSTEP_FAULT_STALL (choosing the parameters).
