docs.title: Manual review notes
docs.text: Guideline How the library complies Dir 4.1 (run-time failures) Every arithmetic operation of the numeric backend saturates; shifts of signed values use sstep_asr(); divisions are by validated non-zero values; the gains are range-checked by sstep_init(). Dir 4.11 (validity of arguments) Every public function checks its pointers and ranges and returns SSTEP_ERR_PARAM; SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS = 0 removes only the NULL checks of sstep_fast_loop(). Dir 4.12, Rule 21.3 (dynamic memory) No heap. Rule 15.5 (single point of exit) One return per function. Rule 17.2 (recursion) No recursion. Rule 21.6 (standard I/O) No <stdio.h>.

docs.title: DEV-01: Rule 11.3 (required), opaque driver instance
docs.text:
• Location: sstep_ctx_of() and sstep_ctx_of_const() in src/sstep_internal.h, the only casts from struct sstep * to struct sstep_ctx *. Marked with cppcheck-suppress misra-c2012-11.3.
  • Rationale: The application allocates the driver instance (no heap, no global state), so it must know its size, but not its layout. The public struct sstep in sstep_ctrl.h is an array of uint64_t of that size; the private struct sstep_ctx holds the state. This keeps the internal types (gains, integrators, setpoints, numeric backend) out of the application code and lets them change without breaking the API.
  • Risk control: sstep_ctrl.c checks at compile time that struct sstep is at least as large and as aligned as struct sstep_ctx; a layout change that outgrows SSTEP_STATE_BYTES does not compile. The application never accesses struct sstep::opaque, so the storage is only ever accessed as struct sstep_ctx. The cast is applied to every public entry point before any member access, and the NULL check is done on its result (a NULL pointer converts to NULL).

docs.title: Motor Control
docs.text: This chapter describes the algorithms of Stepper-C and the equations behind them: the motor model, per-unit scaling, the current controller, microstepping, the motion profile, the voltage limits of the two power stage topologies, the stall detection and the numeric backends. Every number in this chapter comes from the code or from the closed-loop tests on the motor model (tests/unit/gtest_sstep_loop.cpp).

docs.title: Motor model
docs.text:
A two-phase hybrid stepper motor with \(N_s\) full steps per revolution has \(p = N_s / 4\) pole pairs (50 for a 1.8° motor). With the rotor angle \(\theta\) and its speed \(\omega\), each phase is a resistance, an inductance and a back-EMF:

\[ \begin{aligned} v_A &= R\,i_A + L\,\frac{di_A}{dt} - K_t\,\omega \sin(p\theta) \\ v_B &= R\,i_B + L\,\frac{di_B}{dt} + K_t\,\omega \cos(p\theta) \\ T_e &= K_t \left( i_B \cos(p\theta) - i_A \sin(p\theta) \right) \end{aligned} \]

\(K_t\) is the torque constant [N·m/A]; in SI units it equals the back-EMF constant [V·s/rad], the value entered as ke_uv_s_per_rad.

The library imposes the phase currents

\[ i_A = I \cos\varphi \qquad i_B = I \sin\varphi \]

where \(\varphi\) is the electrical angle commanded by the trajectory. The torque becomes

\[ T_e = K_t\, I \sin(\varphi - p\theta) \]

The rotor follows \(\varphi\) with a lag (the load angle) that grows with the load. The motor holds up to \(K_t I\) (0.42 N·m for 2 A with the 17HS19-2004S1) at a load angle of 90° and loses steps above it.

The closed-loop test with a 0.25 N·m load at 1 rev/s measures a load angle of 37.21°, against \(\arcsin(0.25 / 0.4172) = 36.83°\) predicted by the equation; with 0.50 N·m the motor slips, as expected.

docs.title: Per-unit scaling
docs.text:
Internally every signal is a fraction of a base value, so that the same arithmetic works for a 0.5 A and a 10 A motor:

Quantity Base Range inside the loops Current i_full_scale_ma: the current at ADC full scale -1 .. +1 pu Voltage vbus_nominal_mv: the nominal bus voltage -1 .. +1 pu for signals; up to ±65 536 pu in accumulators Bus voltage vbus_nominal_mv 0 .. 2 pu Angle One electrical turn = \(2^{32}\) uint32_t, wraps

sstep_init() converts every engineering value of the configuration into per-unit gains with integer arithmetic (\(2\pi \approx 710 / 113\), error \(8.5 \cdot 10^{-8}\)), so a fixed-point build needs no floating point at all.

docs.title: Microstepping
docs.text:
One full step is a quarter of an electrical turn (\(2^{30}\)). With microsteps \(= M\), one microstep is \(2^{30} / M\) of the 32-bit angle; positions are kept in Q16 microsteps (1/65 536 microstep) in 64 bits, so the angle is exact and never drifts.

The sine and cosine come from a quarter-wave table with linear interpolation (SSTEP_CFG_SINE_TABLE_BITS, default \(2^8\) intervals, 257 entries in flash). Measured worst-case error over a full turn:

Table bits Fixed point Float 6 \(1.08 \cdot 10^{-4}\) (3.5 LSB of Q15) \(7.5 \cdot 10^{-5}\) 8 (default) \(3.1 \cdot 10^{-5}\) (1.0 LSB of Q15) \(4.8 \cdot 10^{-6}\) 10 \(3.1 \cdot 10^{-5}\) (1.0 LSB of Q15) \(3.5 \cdot 10^{-7}\)

With the fixed-point backend the default table is already at the resolution of Q15; a larger table only helps the float backend.

Between two slow-loop periods the fast loop advances the angle by a constant increment, so the current vector turns smoothly at the PWM rate instead of jumping once per millisecond.

docs.title: Current control
docs.text:
Each phase has its own PI controller. The reference comes from the angle and the amplitude, the measurement from the ADC:

\[ e = i_\mathrm{ref} - i_\mathrm{meas} \qquad v = K_p\, e + K_i \int e\, dt + v_\mathrm{ff} \]

Gains. sstep_init() places the zero of the controller on the pole of the winding (\(R / L\)), which leaves an integrator with the crossover frequency \(\omega_c = 2\pi \cdot\) current_bw_hz:

\[ K_p = L\,\omega_c \qquad K_i = R\,\omega_c \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \frac{i_\mathrm{meas}}{i_\mathrm{ref}} = \frac{\omega_c}{s + \omega_c} \]

The closed loop is a first-order low-pass with the requested bandwidth; no manual tuning is needed. The bandwidth must not exceed fast_loop_hz / 4 (checked by sstep_init()).

Back-EMF feed-forward. At speed the motor generates a voltage that the PI would otherwise have to compensate with an error. The library adds it in advance from the commanded speed:

\[ v_{A,\mathrm{ff}} = -K_e\,\omega \sin\varphi \qquad v_{B,\mathrm{ff}} = K_e\,\omega \cos\varphi \qquad \omega = \frac{2\pi\, v}{N_s M} \]

with \(v\) in microsteps/s. With ke_uv_s_per_rad = 0 the feed-forward is off.

Anti-windup. When the requested voltage exceeds what the power stage can apply (see Voltage limits), the integrator is corrected by the difference between the applied and the requested voltage (back-calculation with the tracking time constant \(T_t = L / R\), gain \(T_s R / L\)). The integrator does not wind up while the voltage is limited.

Measured response (17HS19-2004S1, 24 V, 20 kHz, 1 kHz bandwidth, locked rotor, step 0 → 2 A, ADC 12 bits):

Topology Overshoot Rise time 0–90 % Settling ±2 % Final value Full bridge 1.11 % 0.350 ms 0.400 ms 2.0002 A Shared leg 1.11 % 0.350 ms 0.400 ms 1.9999 A

The float backend gives the same numbers within 0.01 %. A first-order system with 1 kHz bandwidth rises to 90 % in \(2.3 / \omega_c = 0.37\) ms; the small overshoot comes from the one-period delay between measurement and PWM update.

docs.title: Voltage drive
docs.text: Boards without current sensing use SSTEP_DRIVE_VOLTAGE: the controller is replaced by \(v = R\, i_\mathrm{ref} + v_\mathrm{ff}\). The current settles at the reference at standstill (test: 2.0 A within 10 mA) but the torque drops at speed, where the inductance and the error of the back-EMF estimate are not corrected. The overcurrent trip is not active in this mode (there is no current measurement).

docs.title: Bus voltage compensation
docs.text: The controllers compute voltages in per unit of the nominal bus voltage. The fast loop converts them to duty cycles with the measured bus voltage (\(V_\mathrm{base} / V_\mathrm{bus}\), updated every slow period), so the phase voltage, and with it the current, does not depend on the supply. Test: with the supply at half its nominal value, the current still settles at 2.0 A within 4 mA.

docs.title: Voltage limits
docs.text:
The two supported topologies differ in how much phase voltage they can apply:

Topology Legs Phase voltages Limit (relative to Vbus) Sinusoidal amplitude SSTEP_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE 4: A+, A−, B+, B− \(v_A = A^+ - A^-\), \(v_B = B^+ - B^-\) \(\max(\lvert v_A \rvert, \lvert v_B \rvert) \le 1\) \(V_\mathrm{bus}\) SSTEP_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG 3: U, V, W (shared) \(v_A = U - W\), \(v_B = V - W\) \(\max(v_A, v_B, 0) - \min(v_A, v_B, 0) \le 1\) about \(V_\mathrm{bus} / \sqrt{2}\)

When the request is beyond the limit, both phase voltages are scaled down by the same factor: the direction of the voltage vector is kept, only its length is reduced, and the anti-windup takes the difference into account.

Duty cycles. Full bridge: each phase is centred at 50 %. Shared leg: the shared leg W is placed in the middle of the available range:

\[ A^{\pm} = \frac{1}{2} \pm \frac{v_A}{2}, \quad B^{\pm} = \frac{1}{2} \pm \frac{v_B}{2} \qquad\qquad W = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{\max(v_A, v_B, 0) + \min(v_A, v_B, 0)}{2}, \quad U = v_A + W, \quad V = v_B + W \]

The fourth compare value is 0 for the shared leg.

Consequence at speed. At 8 rev/s (2 A requested, 24 V) the measured current amplitude is 1.862 A with a full bridge and 1.557 A with a shared leg: the three-leg stage reaches its voltage limit first. Choose the supply voltage for the highest speed of the application.

docs.title: Motion profile
docs.text:
The slow loop advances an integer trajectory once per period; positions are Q16 microsteps (64 bits), velocities Q16 microsteps per period, so a position is exact after any number of moves.

Move (sstep_move_to(), sstep_move_by()). In each period the planner chooses the largest velocity from which it can still stop exactly on the target with the deceleration limit:

\[ v_\mathrm{new} = \frac{-d + \sqrt{d^2 + 8\,d\,\lvert r \rvert - 4\,d\,\lvert v \rvert}}{2} \]

with the deceleration \(d\) and the remaining distance \(r\), both per slow period,

then capped at v_max and changed by at most accel (speeding up) or decel (slowing down) per period. The result is a trapezoid (or a triangle for short moves) that ends on the target with zero velocity, without overshoot. A new target during a move is followed smoothly: there is no velocity step, and a target behind the motor makes it decelerate, reverse and approach from the other side.

Run (sstep_run()). Accelerate or decelerate with the limits to the requested signed velocity and keep it. A reversal passes through zero with decel and then accel.

Stop (sstep_stop()). Decelerate to zero with decel; the target becomes the position where the motor stops.

Measured (16 microsteps, v_max 16 000 microsteps/s, accel 160 000 microsteps/s²): a move of 6 400 microsteps (2 revolutions) ends after 499 ms with the rotor at 6400.00 microsteps and a largest load angle of 10.8°; a reversal from +4 to −4 rev/s stays below a load angle of 8.7°.

Resolution. With slow_loop_hz = 1000 the velocity resolution is \(1000 / 65536 = 0.015\) microsteps/s. sstep_set_motion_limits() rejects values that round to zero or reach \(2^{30}\) Q16 per period.

docs.title: Hold current
docs.text: After hold_delay_ms without motion the current amplitude drops from i_run_ma to i_hold_ma and on_event(SSTEP_EVENT_HOLD_CURRENT) is reported. Any motion switches back to the run current in the same period. The hold current reduces heating at standstill; the holding torque is \(K_t\, i_\mathrm{hold}\).

docs.title: Stall detection
docs.text:
Without an encoder the library does not know where the rotor is. When the load exceeds the torque, the rotor stops following the commanded angle: it stalls at a hard stop, falls behind at speed, or slips under a load that the hold current cannot hold, while the commanded position keeps its value. The stall detector estimates the back-EMF from the quantities the fast loop already has and raises SSTEP_FAULT_STALL when the rotor does not move as commanded. It is off by default (stall_time_ms = 0) and needs SSTEP_DRIVE_CURRENT and ke_uv_s_per_rad > 0.

Reference case. A 17HS19-2004S1 on a three-leg stage at 24 V, 1.5 A run current and 0.5 A hold current after 500 ms, holds a constant 0.12 N·m load at the run current (\(K_t \cdot 1.5 = 0.31\) N·m) but not at the hold current (0.10 N·m). At the run → hold change the rotor slips and spins away; without stall detection the driver stays in SSTEP_STATE_HOLDING with no fault. With the settings below it reports SSTEP_FAULT_STALL 48 ms after the load angle passes 90°.

docs.title: Principle
docs.text:
The winding equation gives the back-EMF from the applied voltage and the measured current. With the convention of the library (\(i_A = I\cos\varphi\), \(i_B = I\sin\varphi\)), the back-EMF of a rotor at the angle \(\theta\) and the speed \(\omega\) is

\[ e_A = -K_e\,\omega \sin(p\theta) \qquad e_B = K_e\,\omega \cos(p\theta) \]

Rotated into the frame of the commanded current (d along the current, q 90° ahead):

\[ e_d = e_A\cos\varphi + e_B\sin\varphi = K_e\,\omega \sin\delta \qquad e_q = -e_A\sin\varphi + e_B\cos\varphi = K_e\,\omega \cos\delta \qquad \delta = \varphi - p\theta \]

The magnitude of the vector is the rotor speed, its angle the load angle \(\delta\).

  • In motion, a synchronous rotor has \(\omega = \omega_c\) and a moderate load angle, so \(e_q \approx K_e\,\omega_c \cos\delta\) is a large constant of the sign of the motion. A stalled rotor gives no back-EMF, so \(e_q\) falls far below \(K_e\,\omega_c\). A rotor that slips turns relative to the commanded frame: the vector rotates, \(e_q\) changes its sign, and the negative half is the sign of the slip. A rotor under load keeps its speed, so a low \(e_q\) comes with a large \(e_d = K_e\,\omega \sin\delta\); that tells it from a blocked rotor.
  • At rest, the commanded frame stands still, so any lasting back-EMF means that the rotor turns. A slipping rotor makes the vector rotate at its electrical speed.

docs.title: Equations
docs.text:
These are the exact operations of the library, in their order, so that a model can reproduce them (Scilab, Python). \(T_s = 1 /\) fast_loop_hz, \(p = N_s / 4\), \(M\) = microsteps; voltages are per unit of vbus_nominal_mv in the fast loop and millivolts in the slow loop.

Fast loop, every period \(k\), after the PI and the voltage limit (phase \(x \in \{A, B\}\)):

\[ \hat e_x[k] = \mathrm{sat}_{\pm 1\,\mathrm{pu}}\!\left( v_x[k-2] - a\, i_x[k] + b\, i_x[k-1] \right) \qquad a = \frac{L}{T_s} + \frac{R}{2} \qquad b = \frac{L}{T_s} - \frac{R}{2} \]

This is \(v - R\,\frac{i[k] + i[k-1]}{2} - L\,\frac{i[k] - i[k-1]}{T_s}\): the winding equation integrated over the period from sample \(k-1\) to \(k\) with the trapezoidal rule, written with two gains computed by sstep_init(). \(v_x[k-2]\) is the phase voltage computed two calls earlier: with the one-period computation delay, the compare values written in call \(k-2\) are applied from sample \(k-1\) to sample \(k\). It is the voltage after the limit of the power stage (what the bridge applies, not the PI output), so the estimate stays valid at the voltage limit.

\[ \hat e_d = \hat e_A\cos\varphi[k] + \hat e_B\sin\varphi[k] \qquad \hat e_q = -\hat e_A\sin\varphi[k] + \hat e_B\cos\varphi[k] \] \[ \bar e_{d,q}[k] = \bar e_{d,q}[k-1] + \frac{T_s}{\tau}\left(\hat e_{d,q}[k] - \bar e_{d,q}[k-1]\right) \]

with \(\tau\) = stall_filter_us. \(\varphi[k]\) is the commanded angle of call \(k\). The voltage was averaged over the period before it, so the estimate refers the rotor at the middle of that period to \(\varphi[k]\): the load angle reads \(\Omega T_s / 2\) more than \(\varphi[k] - p\theta(t_k)\), 0.45° per rev/s at 20 kHz with 50 pole pairs.

Slow loop, every period \(n\), against the command of the slow period that just ended: velocity \(v_c\) [microsteps/s] and its back-EMF \(e_c = K_e\,\omega_c = K_e\,2\pi v_c / (N_s M)\) (the feed-forward value, saturated at 1 pu, converted to mV). \(\bar e_d\), \(\bar e_q\) are the filter outputs rounded to mV.

\[ \text{in motion } (\lvert v_c \rvert \ge v_s): \qquad a = \mathrm{sgn}(v_c)\,\bar e_q \qquad \mathrm{bad} = \left(a < \frac{s}{100}\,\lvert e_c \rvert\right) \;\wedge\; \left(-\frac{\lvert e_c \rvert}{3} - \frac{R I_r}{10} \le \bar e_d \le \frac{\lvert e_c \rvert}{3} + \frac{2 R I_r}{5}\right) \] \[ a < -\left(\frac{\lvert e_c \rvert}{2} + e_s\right) \;\Rightarrow\; h \leftarrow \lfloor N / 2 \rfloor \] \[ \text{at rest or slow } (\lvert v_c \rvert < v_s): \qquad \Delta = (\bar e_d,\; \bar e_q - e_c) \qquad o \leftarrow o + \frac{\Delta - o}{N} \qquad \mathrm{bad} = \lvert \Delta - o \rvert > e_s \] \[ h > 0 \;\Rightarrow\; h \leftarrow h - 1,\;\; \mathrm{bad} \leftarrow \mathrm{true} \qquad\qquad c \leftarrow \begin{cases} c + 1 & \mathrm{bad} \\ \max(c - 1,\, 0) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

and SSTEP_FAULT_STALL when \(c \ge N\), with \(v_s\) = stall_speed, \(s\) = stall_sync_pct, \(N\) = stall_time_ms · slow_loop_hz / 1000, \(I_r\) = i_run_ma and the slip threshold \(e_s = K_e\, 2\pi\, v_s / (N_s M)\) rounded to mV. In integers: \(R I_r\) is in mV, the divisions truncate, \(o\) is held in mV·\(2^{16}\), the update divides with truncation, \(\Delta - o\) uses \(o\) truncated to mV, and the magnitude is compared as a sum of squares. sstep_enable() clears \(\bar e\), \(o\), \(c\), \(h\) and the voltage history (\(v[k-1] = v[k-2] = 0\), \(i[k-1]\) = the last measurement).

Overcurrent: when the trip of the fast loop finds \(c > 0\), the fault is SSTEP_FAULT_OVERCURRENT | SSTEP_FAULT_STALL.

Diagnostics in sstep_get_status(): emf_d_mv and emf_q_mv are \(\bar e_d\), \(\bar e_q\); rotor_velocity is \(\mathrm{sgn}(\bar e_q)\,\lvert \bar e \rvert\, N_s M / (2\pi K_e)\); load_angle_cdeg is \(\mathrm{atan2}(\sigma\bar e_d,\; \sigma\bar e_q)\) with \(\sigma = \mathrm{sgn}(v_c)\) (at rest \(\mathrm{sgn}(\bar e_q)\)), in 0.01°, positive when the rotor lags in the positive direction (the sign of the motor torque); stall_level_pct is \(100\,c / N\).

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Decision Reason Filter in the commanded frame A synchronous back-EMF is constant there at any speed, so a millisecond filter neither attenuates nor delays it. In the phase frame the back-EMF at 10 rev/s is a 500 Hz sine that such a filter would suppress. In motion, \(e_q\) against \(K_e\,\omega_c\) A resistance error (\(R\) of a hot winding) adds \(\Delta R\, I\) along the current, the d axis, and does not change \(e_q\). An inductance error adds \(\Delta L\, I\, p\,\omega\) along q, so the ratio is \(\cos\delta + \Delta L\, I\, p / K_e\) at every speed (the second term is −0.22 for \(L\) −20 % at 1.5 A, −0.29 at 2 A). Window on \(e_d\) The \(L\) error alone brings a rotor under load down to the threshold: at 2 A and \(L\) −20 % a ratio of 0.30 means only \(\delta \approx 54°\). A blocked rotor has only the resistance error on d, mostly positive and, for \(R\) between −10 % and +40 %, inside the window. A rotor under load is outside it at speed; at low speed the outcome depends on the sign of the motion and on \(\Delta R\), so the margin is wider going forward on a hot winding. Reversed back-EMF holds the condition The vector of a slipping rotor is above any threshold on \(e_q\) for about half of each turn, so the up/down counter alone stays low. \(a < -(\lvert e_c \rvert / 2 + e_s)\) means \(\delta\) beyond about 120°: no equilibrium exists there. It keeps the condition true for \(N / 2\) periods, a turn of the vector faster than that accumulates at full rate, and a single event ends at 50 % of the trip. Threshold relative to \(K_e\,\omega_c\) The synchronous value \(\cos\delta\) does not depend on the speed; a fixed fraction separates a loaded synchronous rotor from a stall (about 0, ±0.29 with the \(L\) error at 2 A). Stall flag on the overcurrent trip A light rotor torn away by a large load reaches the trip in less than stall_time_ms, because the back-EMF of a rotor spinning backwards exceeds the bus. The flag tells the application that the position is lost. It only needs the detector to have started (\(c > 0\)), so it can also appear with an overcurrent of another cause during a transient. At rest, learned offset A resting rotor has no back-EMF, so a constant estimate is an observer error: \(\Delta R\, I\), the dead-time voltage, current-sensor offsets (0.91 V at 1.5 A in the worst case below, more than the threshold). Its running mean is subtracted. A slipping rotor makes the vector rotate, which averages out of the mean and stays in \(\Delta - o\). Offset time constant = trip time An offset that appears at once (enable, run → hold) decays below \(e_s\) after \(N \ln(\text{offset} / e_s)\) periods. That is less than \(N\) for an offset below \(e \cdot e_s\) (2.7 times the threshold), so it never trips. A slip at \(\Omega \gg 1 / T_N\) (\(T_N\) = stall_time_ms) passes the mean unchanged. Below \(v_s\), deviation from \((0, e_c)\) The motor may move slowly right after sstep_enable(), without a rest period to learn the offset: the deviation from the expected back-EMF has the same zero mean at rest and in slow motion. Up/down counter A stall keeps the condition true: the fault comes \(N\) slow periods after it begins. Short events (enable, current steps, resonance, reversal through zero) count down again; a condition true less than half of the time does not accumulate. Decision in the slow loop The fast loop only estimates and filters; the comparison, the offset tracking and the counter run at 1 kHz on integer millivolts, identical in both numeric backends.

docs.title: Choosing the parameters
docs.text: Field Example (17HS19, ESC1) How to choose stall_time_ms 50 Detection delay after the stall; longer is more robust. Keep an offset at rest below \(e \cdot e_s\) (see above). stall_filter_us 1000 0.5 to 2 ms. Shorter follows faster slips but passes more current quantization noise: one ADC count changes \(\hat e\) by \(L\,\Delta i / \tau\) (87 mV for 29 mA at 1 ms). A rotating vector is filtered to at most \(K_e / (p\,\tau)\) (4.2 V at 1 ms), which must stay well above \(e_s\). stall_speed 1600 (0.5 rev/s, \(e_s\) = 655 mV) Above the back-EMF noise at rest; the commanded speed from which the synchronism check runs. stall_sync_pct 50 Above \(\lvert\Delta L\rvert\, I\, p / K_e\), the value a blocked rotor shows with a larger inductance than configured (29 % at \(L\) +20 %, 2 A). A rotor under load with \(e_d\) inside the window must stay above it: at 50 %, with the nominal \(R\) and \(L\), that ends at \(\delta\) = 60°, 87 % of the pull-out torque. The window accepts the lag at the voltage limit, so this value also runs at 11 rev/s on a 24 V three-leg stage.

docs.title: Measured on the motor model
docs.text:
Tests SstepLoop.Stall* and SstepStall.* with the example settings, fixed point and float backend alike. The worst-case plant differs from the configuration as a real board does: \(R\) +30 % (hot winding), \(L\) −20 % (saturation), 70 mV dead-time error per leg (24 V, 20 kHz), ESC1 current quantization (29 mA per count instead of 2 mA) and a detent torque of 0.02 N·m.

Case Result Reference case, 0.12 N·m at the hold current (nominal and worst-case plant) SSTEP_FAULT_STALL 48 ms after the load angle passes 90° Rotor blocked at 3 rev/s (hard stop), either direction, both topologies, worst case SSTEP_FAULT_STALL after 50.0 ms Rotor turning at 1 rev/s with the command at rest SSTEP_FAULT_STALL after 50.0 ms Rotor imposed at 3 rev/s \(\lvert \bar e \rvert\) 3936 mV against \(K_e\,\omega\) = 3932 mV; rotor_velocity 9609 microsteps/s for 9600; load angle 10.27° (model 10.28°) Enable, run → hold, 0.07 N·m through run → hold, 6400-microstep move, reversal ±4 rev/s and stop, runs at 0.125, 0.25, 0.47, 1, 2, 8, 9.5 and 11 rev/s No fault. Largest detector level 6 % (nominal plant), 32 % (worst case) Heavy axis, 0.5 N·m load step above the pull-out torque, \(J\) ×20 and ×100 at 1 and 3 rev/s, either direction, nominal and worst case SSTEP_FAULT_STALL 43 to 60 ms after the load angle passes 90°, 23 to 158 full steps lost Bare rotor and \(J\) ×5, the same load step at 1 rev/s: the overcurrent trip comes first SSTEP_FAULT_OVERCURRENT \| SSTEP_FAULT_STALL, 14 and 78 full steps lost 0.30 N·m (72 % of the pull-out torque) at ±1, ±2 and ±3 rev/s, \(R\) +30 %, \(L\) −20 %; 0.25 N·m at ±1 rev/s, worst case No fault. Largest detector level 40 % and 58 % Voltage limit: 8 rev/s at 18 V, 9 rev/s at 20 V, 11 rev/s at 24 V with \(L\) +20 % No fault. Largest detector level 0 %

The motor model of this repository shows no sustained mid-band oscillation between 8 and 11 rev/s; those runs check the voltage limit and the current lag. A 0.09 N·m load at the run → hold change is a real slip in the model (the undamped rotor overshoots past 90°) and is reported.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
Fixed point Float Fast loop, added per period 4 gain multiplications, 4 Q15 multiplications, 2 filter updates, 10 saturating additions Same operations in float Fast loop, executed instructions without / with stall detection (-Os) 1030 / 1502 726 / 940 Same with -O2 664 / 909 683 / 923 Slow loop, added 367 instructions (-Os) 318 instructions sstep_get_status() 1202 instructions (-Os; integer CORDIC and square root) 1148 RAM per instance, added 96 B (Cortex-M4) 96 B

Instructions counted on a Cortex-M4 image (GCC 15.2) in an instruction-set emulator, mean over 600 fast-loop periods while accelerating to 3 rev/s; on Cortex-M4 most of them take one cycle. At 170 MHz and 20 kHz the observer takes about 1.5 µs (-O2) to 2.8 µs (fixed point, -Os) of the 50 µs period. With stall_time_ms = 0 the fast loop skips the observer (one comparison).

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Below stall_speed, a rotor that stops while the command creeps slowly is not seen: its back-EMF is close to zero either way. Only a rotor faster than the command is.
  • The fault comes stall_time_ms after the stall begins; the position is lost from the beginning of the stall.
  • A rotor under load near the voltage limit whose load angle repeatedly swings beyond about 120° is reported, even if it has not lost a step yet (11 rev/s at 20 V: fault 74 to 78 ms after the angle first passes 90°, largest angle 137° to 140° until then). This operating point has no margin; lower the speed or raise the voltage.
  • On a hot winding with \(L\) −20 % at low speed, going backward, \(e_d\) of a rotor under load is close to that of a blocked rotor. There the margin comes from stall_sync_pct alone (the formula above).
  • During a slip at rest rotor_velocity is low (the filter attenuates the rotating vector: about 10 000 for 27 000 microsteps/s); it is accurate in synchronism. An inductance error biases it too (26 700 for 31 400 microsteps/s with \(L\) −20 % at 10 rev/s).
  • The observer needs the phase currents (SSTEP_DRIVE_CURRENT) and \(K_e\).
  • Verified on the motor model of the tests; the closed-loop validation with the sfs-stepper-sim plant and on hardware follows.

docs.title: Numeric backends
docs.text:
Fixed point Float Select SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND=FIXED (default) SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND=FLOAT Signals Q15 in int16_t float Accumulators Q15 in int32_t (±65 536) float, clamped to the same range Integrators Q27 in int32_t (±16 pu) float, clamped to ±16 Gains Q15 mantissa and power-of-two exponent (−16 .. 15) float Arithmetic Saturating; rounding half up; no undefined shifts Saturating to the same ranges Typical target Cortex-M0/M0+/M3, RISC-V without F extension Cortex-M4F/M7/M33 with FPU, STM32G4

Both backends saturate at the same limits, so the control behaves the same; the unit tests and the closed-loop tests run against both. The motion planner and the configuration are integer code in both backends.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Stepper-C is a C11 library that drives a two-phase hybrid stepper motor with closed-loop sinusoidal current control. Given the measured phase currents and bus voltage, it computes the PWM compare values of the power stage, and it turns motion commands (move to a position, run at a velocity, stop) into a smooth microstep trajectory. It runs on any MCU: the hardware is reached only through callbacks, and the numeric backend is either fixed point (no FPU needed) or single-precision float.

docs.title: What the library does
docs.text:
• Controls the phase currents. One PI controller per phase with back-EMF feed-forward and anti-windup, gains derived from the motor's R and L and the requested bandwidth. An open-loop voltage mode is available for boards without current sensing.
  • Generates the microstep angle. Sine/cosine current references from a 32-bit electrical angle, 1 to 256 microsteps per full step.
  • Plans the motion. Trapezoidal profile with separate acceleration and deceleration, no overshoot, smooth replacement of a running command; constant-velocity mode; stop.
  • Fits the voltage to the power stage. Two full H-bridges (4 legs) or three half-bridges with a shared leg (3 legs); the request is limited to what the topology and the measured bus voltage can deliver, keeping its direction.
  • Protects the hardware. Overcurrent, overvoltage and undervoltage trips in the fast loop, hardware-callback errors, external faults; outputs off within the same period.
  • Detects a stall without a sensor. A back-EMF observer reports a rotor that stops, falls out of synchronism or slips at standstill (SSTEP_FAULT_STALL, optional).
  • Reduces the current at standstill. Hold current after a configurable delay.

docs.title: What the library does not do
docs.text: Concern Why it is not in the library Timer, PWM and ADC drivers Hardware-specific; you start the conversions and pass raw ADC counts in, and write the compare values out in a callback. Interrupt and task setup Every system has its own; the library only defines which function runs at which rate. See the integration guide. Position feedback (encoder) The library is an open-loop positioner with closed-loop current; the rotor position is not measured. Sensorless stall detection reports a lost synchronism but does not correct the position. Homing, limit switches, G-code, multi-axis coordination Application logic on top of sstep_move_to(), sstep_set_position() and the status. Motor parameter identification R, L and Kt come from the datasheet or a measurement. Communication (UART, CAN, Modbus…) Out of scope; call the API from your protocol handler.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text:
• Firmware for stepper drives on a general-purpose MCU with gate drivers, for example STMicroelectronics B-G431B-ESC1 or a custom board with two H-bridges.
  • Machines with several axes, one driver instance per motor, no shared state.
  • Projects that must be reviewed or certified: MISRA C:2012, 100 % coverage, no heap, bounded execution time.

docs.title: Key properties
docs.text: Property Value Language C11, no warnings with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion Dependencies <stddef.h>, <stdint.h>, <stdbool.h> only Numeric backends Fixed point Q15/Q31 (integer only) or single-precision float, chosen at build time Memory No heap, no global or static mutable data (.data and .bss are empty) RAM per instance 432 B fixed point, 456 B float on Cortex-M4 (details) Flash 9.0 KiB fixed point, 9.7 KiB float (Cortex-M4, -Os, both topologies) Stack sstep_fast_loop() 216 B, sstep_slow_loop() 152 B worst case (Cortex-M4 -Os, details) Coding standard MISRA C:2012, 0 Cppcheck addon violations, 1 deviation Tests 100 % line and branch coverage of src/ in both backends; closed-loop tests on a motor model Thread safety One fast-loop context and one slow-loop context per instance, by design; see Threading License Apache License 2.0

docs.title: Terminology
docs.text: Full step 1/200 of a revolution for a 1.8° motor; a quarter of an electrical period. Microstep A full step divided by microsteps (power of two, 1 to 256). Positions and velocities of the API are in microsteps. Electrical angle Angle of the current vector in the two phases; one electrical period is four full steps. Held as a 32-bit unsigned number, one turn = \(2^{32}\). Per unit (pu) Internal signals are relative to a base value: currents to i_full_scale_ma, voltages to vbus_nominal_mv. 1.0 pu is the base. Fast loop sstep_fast_loop(), called from the PWM/ADC interrupt at fast_loop_hz (typically 20 kHz): current control and PWM. Slow loop sstep_slow_loop(), called at slow_loop_hz (typically 1 kHz): trajectory, angle, currents, events. Leg One half-bridge (high-side and low-side switch) of the power stage, driven by one PWM compare value. Load angle Electrical angle between the commanded current vector and the rotor; it grows with the load torque and the motor loses steps when it exceeds 90° (180° to the next stable position).

docs.title: Conventions in this documentation
docs.text:
• Engineering units in the API are integers with the unit in the field name: _mohm, _uh, _ma, _mv, _hz, _ms, _ns.
  • "Fixed point" and "float" name the two numeric backends; numbers are given for both when they differ.
  • The example motor is a 17HS19-2004S1 (1.6 Ω, 3.0 mH, 2.0 A, 0.21 N·m/A, 200 steps) on a 24 V supply; the example board is a B-G431B-ESC1 (three half-bridges).

docs.title: Using the Library
docs.text: This chapter shows how to bring a motor up with Stepper-C: fill the configuration, start the driver, command motion, read the status and handle faults. The hardware side (timer, ADC, interrupts) is in the Integration Guide; the meaning of every configuration field is in Configuration.

docs.title: Setting up a driver
docs.text:
One struct sstep controls one motor. Allocate it statically (or in any memory that lives as long as the motor runs), fill a struct sstep_config and call sstep_init():

static struct sstep motor;

int motor_start(const struct sstep_config* cfg)
{
    int result = sstep_init(&motor, cfg);
    if (result == SSTEP_OK)
    {
        result = sstep_enable(&motor);
    }
    return result;
}

sstep_init() checks every field, derives the controller gains, the ADC scaling, the trip levels and the motion constants, and leaves the outputs off (SSTEP_STATE_DISABLED). It does not call any callback. Start the PWM timer and the ADC before sstep_enable(): the fast loop must already run when the outputs are switched on.

sstep_enable() calls output_enable(true) and holds the current position with the run current (the hold current follows after hold_delay_ms). The rotor jumps to the nearest position of the commanded electrical angle when the current appears: up to two full steps on the first enable after power-up.

docs.title: Commanding motion
docs.text:
All motion commands take positions in microsteps and return immediately; the slow loop executes them. They are accepted in SSTEP_STATE_HOLDING and SSTEP_STATE_MOVING.

Command Effect sstep_move_to(&motor, 3200) Move to the absolute position 3200 with the trapezoidal profile sstep_move_by(&motor, -800) Move 800 microsteps back from the current target sstep_run(&motor, 6400) Accelerate to 6400 microsteps/s and keep running (negative: other direction) sstep_stop(&motor) Decelerate to standstill and hold sstep_set_position(&motor, 0) Call the current position 0 (homing); only at standstill, the rotor does not move sstep_set_motion_limits(&motor, v_max, accel, decel) New limits, used from the next slow period sstep_set_current(&motor, run_ma, hold_ma) New run and hold currents

A command replaces the running one without a velocity step: a new target during a move, a run during a move, a reversal during a run. sstep_move_by() adds to the target, so several relative moves given in a row add up.

Wait for a move with the event callback or by polling the status:

static volatile bool move_done;

static void on_event(void* context, enum sstep_event event)
{
    (void)context;
    if (event == SSTEP_EVENT_MOVE_DONE)
    {
        move_done = true;
    }
}

bool motor_is_idle(void)
{
    struct sstep_status st;
    return (sstep_get_status(&motor, &st) == SSTEP_OK) && (st.state == SSTEP_STATE_HOLDING);
}

docs.title: Reading the status
docs.text:
sstep_get_status() fills a snapshot in engineering units:

Field Unit Meaning state – SSTEP_STATE_DISABLED, …_HOLDING, …_MOVING, …_FAULT faults flags Active SSTEP_FAULT_… flags position microsteps Commanded position (rounded) target microsteps Target of the current move velocity microsteps/s Commanded velocity i_a_ma, i_b_ma mA Last measured phase currents vbus_mv mV Last measured bus voltage emf_d_mv, emf_q_mv mV Back-EMF estimate along and 90° ahead of the commanded current (stall detection) rotor_velocity microsteps/s Rotor velocity estimated from the back-EMF (stall detection) load_angle_cdeg 0.01° Estimated load angle in motion (stall detection) stall_level_pct % Stall detector level; the fault comes at 100

Position and velocity are commanded values. There is no encoder: with stall detection the library reports a rotor that stops following the command (next section); without it a lost step goes unnoticed. Either way, keep the load angle reserve with enough current and a sensible acceleration (Motor Control).

docs.title: Detecting a stall
docs.text:
Stall detection estimates the back-EMF of the motor in the fast loop and raises SSTEP_FAULT_STALL when the rotor stops in motion, falls out of synchronism, or turns while the command is at rest (for example a load that the hold current cannot hold). It is off unless stall_time_ms is set, and needs current drive and ke_uv_s_per_rad:

static struct sstep_config with_stall_detection(struct sstep_config cfg)
{
    cfg.ctrl.stall_time_ms = 50U;     /* report after 50 ms */
    cfg.ctrl.stall_filter_us = 1000U; /* back-EMF filter */
    cfg.ctrl.stall_speed = 1600U;     /* 0.5 rev/s at 16 microsteps: slip threshold */
    cfg.ctrl.stall_sync_pct = 50U;    /* in motion: back-EMF >= 50 % of Ke * speed */
    return cfg;
}

The fault is handled like the others (next section): the outputs are off and the commanded position no longer matches the rotor, so home the axis again after sstep_clear_faults(). Below stall_speed only a rotor faster than the command is detected; run homing moves against a hard stop faster than stall_speed.

While tuning, log the estimates from the slow-loop context and look at the margin: stall_level_pct should stay well below 100 in every normal operating point, and load_angle_cdeg shows how much torque reserve is left.

void log_stall_margin(void)
{
    struct sstep_status st;
    if (sstep_get_status(&motor, &st) == SSTEP_OK)
    {
        board_log_stall(st.velocity, st.rotor_velocity, st.load_angle_cdeg, st.stall_level_pct);
    }
}

The algorithm, the choice of the four values and the measured results are in Stall detection.

docs.title: Handling faults
docs.text:
A fault switches the outputs off at once, sets SSTEP_STATE_FAULT and calls on_fault() with the new flags. Commands then return SSTEP_ERR_STATE.

Flag Raised by Typical cause SSTEP_FAULT_OVERCURRENT Fast loop, current drive only Short circuit, wrong adc_i_span sign, gains far too high SSTEP_FAULT_OVERVOLTAGE Fast loop Regenerated energy when braking a load; supply too high SSTEP_FAULT_UNDERVOLTAGE Fast loop Supply off or sagging; vbus_min_mv too close to nominal SSTEP_FAULT_HAL Any function that calls a callback pwm_write() or output_enable() returned a negative value SSTEP_FAULT_EXTERNAL (or any flag you choose) sstep_report_fault() Gate driver fault pin, over-temperature SSTEP_FAULT_STALL Slow loop, stall detection on; fast loop, with SSTEP_FAULT_OVERCURRENT, when the rotor is torn away faster than stall_time_ms Load above the torque, hard stop, rotor slipping at the hold current

Report a gate driver fault from its interrupt:

void EXTI15_10_IRQHandler(void);
void EXTI15_10_IRQHandler(void)
{
    if (board_driver_fault())
    {
        (void)sstep_report_fault(&motor, SSTEP_FAULT_EXTERNAL);
    }
}

To recover, remove the cause, then:

if ((sstep_clear_faults(&motor) == SSTEP_OK) && (sstep_enable(&motor) == SSTEP_OK))
{
    board_led(false);
}

sstep_clear_faults() returns to SSTEP_STATE_DISABLED; the position is kept, so the motor continues from where it was commanded (it may have been moved by hand meanwhile).

docs.title: Several motors
docs.text:
Each motor has its own instance and its own callbacks; use context to tell the callbacks which hardware they drive:

static struct sstep axes[2];
static const uint32_t axis_ids[2] = {0U, 1U};

static int axis_pwm_write(void* context, const uint16_t compare[SSTEP_LEGS_MAX])
{
    board_pwm_set_axis(*(const uint32_t*)context, compare);
    return 0;
}

with .hal.context = (void*)&axis_ids[k] in the configuration of axis k. The fast loops of several axes may run in one interrupt one after the other, or in separate interrupts.

docs.title: Return values
docs.text:
Code Value Returned when SSTEP_OK 0 Success SSTEP_ERR_PARAM −1 NULL pointer, a value outside its range, |velocity| > v_max, a relative move that overflows SSTEP_ERR_CONFIG −2 Configuration fields that do not fit together, currents above the trip or rated current SSTEP_ERR_STATE −3 Any function but sstep_init() on an instance without a successful sstep_init(); a motion command while disabled or faulted; sstep_set_position() while moving; sstep_enable() while faulted SSTEP_ERR_UNSUPPORTED −4 A topology that is not compiled in

sstep_fast_loop() returns SSTEP_ERR_PARAM only for NULL arguments and only with SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS = 1; its faults are reported through the state and on_fault().

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause SSTEP_FAULT_OVERCURRENT right after sstep_enable() adc_i_span has the wrong sign (inverting amplifier) or adc_i_zero is wrong: the controller sees the current in the wrong direction and drives it up SSTEP_FAULT_UNDERVOLTAGE right after sstep_enable() The fast loop ran before the first ADC conversion (vbus = 0), or adc_vbus_mv_full is wrong The motor hums but does not turn Phases swapped or one phase reversed; current_bw_hz too low; v_max above what the supply can drive The motor turns the wrong way Swap the two wires of one phase, or negate positions in the application Loses steps at speed Not enough voltage for the speed (Voltage limits); shared-leg stage at its limit; acceleration too high for the load Moves are jerky, about once per millisecond sstep_slow_loop() is not called at slow_loop_hz, or fast_loop_hz does not match the real interrupt rate Current settles at the wrong value i_full_scale_ma / adc_i_span do not match the shunt and amplifier SSTEP_FAULT_STALL at enable or at the run → hold change, rotor at rest Observer offset above \(e\) times the slip threshold (wrong r_mohm, adc_i_zero): check emf_d_mv at rest, raise stall_speed SSTEP_FAULT_STALL at speed although the motor runs Load close to the pull-out torque, or a load angle swinging beyond about 120° near the voltage limit: check load_angle_cdeg, lower stall_sync_pct for a heavy load (not below the inductance error, Choosing the parameters), lower the speed or raise the current sstep_init() returns SSTEP_ERR_CONFIG Check the combinations: trip ≤ full scale, run current ≤ trip and rated, bandwidth ≤ fast_loop_hz / 4, fast_loop_hz a multiple of slow_loop_hz

docs.text: Type Name int sstep_clear_faults (struct sstep * drv) Clear all faults; the driver goes to SSTEP_STATE_DISABLED . int sstep_disable (struct sstep * drv) Stop immediately and switch the outputs off (motor coasts, no holding torque). int sstep_enable (struct sstep * drv) Enable the outputs and hold the current position with the hold current. int sstep_fast_loop (struct sstep * drv, const struct sstep_sample * sample) Fast loop: convert the measurements, run the current controllers, limit the voltage, map it to the legs of the topology and write the PWM. int sstep_get_status (const struct sstep * drv, struct sstep_status * status) Read a status snapshot in engineering units. int sstep_init (struct sstep * drv, const struct sstep_config * cfg) Validate a configuration and initialise a driver. int sstep_move_by (struct sstep * drv, int32_t delta) Start a move relative to the current target. int sstep_move_to (struct sstep * drv, int32_t position) Start a move to an absolute position with the trapezoidal profile. int sstep_report_fault (struct sstep * drv, uint16_t faults) Report a fault detected by the application (driver fault pin, temperature). int sstep_run (struct sstep * drv, int32_t velocity) Run at a constant velocity (accelerating with the configured limits) until another command. int sstep_set_current (struct sstep * drv, uint32_t run_ma, uint32_t hold_ma) Change the run and hold currents. int sstep_set_motion_limits (struct sstep * drv, uint32_t v_max, uint32_t accel, uint32_t decel) Change the motion limits; they apply from the next sstep_slow_loop() , also to a running command. int sstep_set_position (struct sstep * drv, int32_t position) Redefine the current position (homing). int sstep_slow_loop (struct sstep * drv) Slow loop: advance the trajectory, update the angle and current references, handle the hold current and report events. int sstep_stop (struct sstep * drv) Decelerate to standstill with the configured deceleration and hold.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Execution model. One driver instance (struct sstep) controls one motor. The application calls two functions periodically:

Function Rate Context Work sstep_fast_loop() fast_loop_hz (PWM rate or an integer fraction of it) PWM / ADC interrupt current control, voltage limit, topology mapping, PWM write sstep_slow_loop() slow_loop_hz (typically 1 kHz) main loop or a timer task trajectory, microstep angle, hold current, fault handling

All other functions are called from the same context as sstep_slow_loop(). The library never reads a clock, never blocks, allocates no memory and has no global state: time is given by the configured loop rates.

Hardware access is done only through the callbacks in sstep_callbacks, given once to sstep_init(). Measurements are passed to sstep_fast_loop() as raw ADC counts.

Initialization. Every function except sstep_init() returns SSTEP_ERR_STATE for an instance without a successful sstep_init() (a zeroed instance, or one whose last sstep_init() failed in the derivation of the constants), and touches no hardware. sstep_fast_loop() checks this only when SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS is 1.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Every macro has a default and may be overridden in one of two ways: * on the compiler command line (-DSSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND=SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FLOAT), or * in a user header sstep_user_config.h, included when the macro SSTEP_USER_CONFIG is defined (CMake: set SSTEP_CONFIG_DIR to its folder).

Values that cannot change at run time (code size, table sizes, which code paths exist) live here. Motor and board parameters are run-time values passed to sstep_init().

docs.title: define SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS
docs.text:
1: every public function validates its pointer arguments (MISRA Dir 4.11). 

#define SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS `1`

0 removes the checks from sstep_fast_loop() only, the function called from the PWM interrupt; all other functions always check.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Units. Configuration values are integers in engineering units (milliohm, microhenry, milliampere, millivolt, hertz, nanosecond) so that sstep_init() needs no floating point with the fixed point backend. The unit is part of every field name (r_mohm, l_uh...). Positions are in microsteps, velocities in microsteps per second.

Sign convention. A positive phase voltage drives a positive phase current; positive velocity increases the position. Phase A leads phase B by 90 electrical degrees for positive motion.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
The control code is written once against these types and operations; the backend is selected at build time with SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND.

Per-unit signals. Inside the control loops every electrical signal is normalised to a base value computed by sstep_init(): * current: 1.0 = power stage current full scale (i_full_scale_ma), * voltage: 1.0 = nominal bus voltage (vbus_nominal_mv), * duty cycle: 1.0 = 100 %.

Both backends therefore see values in about -1..+1, which makes Q15 exact enough and lets the two backends be compared sample by sample in the tests.

Type Fixed point backend Float backend sstep_real_t int16_t, Q15 (1.0 = 32768, range -1 .. +0.99997) float, same range sstep_acc_t int32_t, Q15 with 16 integer bits (range +/-65536) float, same range sstep_angle_t uint32_t, one electrical turn = 2^32 same struct sstep_gain Q15 mantissa and binary exponent float

Same behaviour in both backends. Every operation saturates to the ranges in the table instead of overflowing, in both backends, so that a test can compare them. Angles wrap by design.

Speed. The per-sample operations are static inline and branch-light; the fixed point backend uses only 32-bit multiplications (no 64-bit arithmetic), so it suits Cortex-M0. Functions that convert engineering units (*_from_ratio, sstep_real_to_units()) use 64-bit integers and division: call them at initialisation or from the slow loop, not from the fast loop.

docs.title: function sstep_gain_from_ratio
docs.text:
Create a gain equal to num / den. 

int sstep_gain_from_ratio (
    int32_t num,
    int32_t den,
    struct sstep_gain * gain
)

Initialisation only (64-bit division).

Parameters:

  • num Numerator.
  • den Denominator, not 0.
  • gain Result.

Return value:

  • SSTEP_OK Success.
  • SSTEP_ERR_PARAM gain is NULL, den is 0, or |num / den| rounds above 32767.

Note:

Every non-zero int32 ratio is at least 2^-31 and is representable; ratios below 2^-16 lose resolution (the mantissa is no longer normalised).

docs.text:
Create a gain equal to num / den with 64-bit operands, for gains computed from several engineering values (for example L * wc * I_base / V_base). 

int sstep_gain_from_ratio64 (
    int64_t num,
    int64_t den,
    struct sstep_gain * gain
)

Initialisation and slow loop only: at most three 64-bit divisions.

Parameters:

  • num Numerator, |num| < 2^62.
  • den Denominator, 0 < |den| < 2^62.
  • gain Result.

Return value:

  • SSTEP_OK (gain NULL, den 0, an operand out of range, or |num / den| rounds above 32767). Ratios below 2^-31 give 0 (fixed point).

#ifndef SSTEP_CONFIG_H
#define SSTEP_CONFIG_H

/* ==============================================================================
 * INCLUDES
 * =============================================================================*/

#ifdef SSTEP_USER_CONFIG
#include "sstep_user_config.h"
#endif

/* ==============================================================================
 * NUMERIC BACKEND
 * =============================================================================*/

#define SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FIXED 0

#define SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FLOAT 1

#ifndef SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND
#define SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FIXED
#endif

#if (SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND != SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FIXED) && \
    (SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND != SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FLOAT)
#error "SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND must be SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FIXED or SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FLOAT"
#endif

/* ==============================================================================
 * POWER STAGE TOPOLOGIES
 * =============================================================================*/

#ifndef SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE
#define SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE 1
#endif

#ifndef SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG
#define SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG 1
#endif

#if (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE != 0) && (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE != 1)
#error "SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE must be 0 or 1"
#endif

#if (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG != 0) && (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG != 1)
#error "SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG must be 0 or 1"
#endif

#if (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE == 0) && (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG == 0)
#error "At least one power stage topology must be enabled"
#endif

/* ==============================================================================
 * MICROSTEPPING
 * =============================================================================*/

#ifndef SSTEP_CFG_MICROSTEPS_MAX
#define SSTEP_CFG_MICROSTEPS_MAX 256U
#endif

#if (SSTEP_CFG_MICROSTEPS_MAX < 1U) || (SSTEP_CFG_MICROSTEPS_MAX > 256U) || \
    ((SSTEP_CFG_MICROSTEPS_MAX & (SSTEP_CFG_MICROSTEPS_MAX - 1U)) != 0U)
#error "SSTEP_CFG_MICROSTEPS_MAX must be a power of two in 1..256"
#endif

#ifndef SSTEP_CFG_SINE_TABLE_BITS
#define SSTEP_CFG_SINE_TABLE_BITS 8U
#endif

#if (SSTEP_CFG_SINE_TABLE_BITS < 6U) || (SSTEP_CFG_SINE_TABLE_BITS > 10U)
#error "SSTEP_CFG_SINE_TABLE_BITS must be in 6..10"
#endif

/* ==============================================================================
 * RUN-TIME CHECKS
 * =============================================================================*/

#ifndef SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS
#define SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS 1
#endif

#if (SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS != 0) && (SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS != 1)
#error "SSTEP_CFG_ARG_CHECKS must be 0 or 1"
#endif

#endif /* SSTEP_CONFIG_H */

docs.title: typedef sstep_output_enable_fn
docs.text:
Enable or disable the power stage outputs (disabled = all legs high impedance). 

typedef int(* sstep_output_enable_fn) (void *context, bool enable);

Parameters:

  • context sstep_callbacks::context.
  • enable true to enable the gate drivers, false to switch every leg off.

Return value:

  • 0 Success.
  • <0 Error, reported as SSTEP_FAULT_HAL.

docs.title: typedef sstep_pwm_write_fn
docs.text:
Write the PWM compare values of all legs. 

typedef int(* sstep_pwm_write_fn) (void *context, const uint16_t compare[SSTEP_LEGS_MAX]);

Called from sstep_fast_loop().

Parameters:

  • context sstep_callbacks::context.
  • compare One compare value per leg, 0 .. pwm_period_ticks (0 = low-side on, pwm_period_ticks = high-side on). Entries above the leg count of the topology are 0. Valid only during the call.

Return value:

  • 0 Success.
  • <0 Error: the driver switches the outputs off with SSTEP_FAULT_HAL.

#ifndef SSTEP_CTRL_H
#define SSTEP_CTRL_H

/* ==============================================================================
 * INCLUDES
 * =============================================================================*/

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "sstep_config.h"
#include "sstep_defs.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* ==============================================================================
 * CALLBACK TYPES
 * =============================================================================*/

typedef int (*sstep_pwm_write_fn)(void* context, const uint16_t compare[SSTEP_LEGS_MAX]);

typedef int (*sstep_output_enable_fn)(void* context, bool enable);

typedef void (*sstep_fault_fn)(void* context, uint16_t faults);

enum sstep_event
{
    SSTEP_EVENT_MOVE_DONE = 0,   
    SSTEP_EVENT_HOLD_CURRENT = 1 
};

typedef void (*sstep_event_fn)(void* context, enum sstep_event event);

/* ==============================================================================
 * CONFIGURATION TYPES
 * =============================================================================*/

struct sstep_callbacks
{
    void* context;                        
    sstep_pwm_write_fn pwm_write;         
    sstep_output_enable_fn output_enable; 
    sstep_fault_fn on_fault;              
    sstep_event_fn on_event;              
};

struct sstep_motor_cfg
{
    uint32_t r_mohm;             
    uint32_t l_uh;               
    uint32_t i_rated_ma;         
    uint32_t ke_uv_s_per_rad;    
    uint16_t full_steps_per_rev; 
};

struct sstep_stage_cfg
{
    enum sstep_topology topology; 
    uint32_t vbus_nominal_mv;     
    uint32_t vbus_min_mv;         
    uint32_t vbus_max_mv;         
    uint32_t i_full_scale_ma;     
    uint32_t i_trip_ma;           
    uint16_t pwm_period_ticks;    
    uint32_t pwm_freq_hz;         
    uint32_t dead_time_ns;        
    uint16_t adc_i_zero;          
    int32_t adc_i_span;           
    uint32_t adc_vbus_mv_full;    
    uint16_t adc_full;            
};

enum sstep_drive_mode
{
    SSTEP_DRIVE_CURRENT = 0,
    SSTEP_DRIVE_VOLTAGE = 1
};

struct sstep_ctrl_cfg
{
    enum sstep_drive_mode drive_mode; 
    uint32_t fast_loop_hz;            
    uint32_t slow_loop_hz;            
    uint16_t microsteps;              
    uint32_t current_bw_hz;           
    uint32_t i_run_ma;                
    uint32_t i_hold_ma;               
    uint32_t hold_delay_ms;           
    uint32_t v_max;                   
    uint32_t accel;                   
    uint32_t decel;                   
    uint32_t stall_time_ms;           
    uint32_t stall_filter_us;         
    uint32_t stall_speed;             
    uint16_t stall_sync_pct;          
};

struct sstep_config
{
    struct sstep_motor_cfg motor; 
    struct sstep_stage_cfg stage; 
    struct sstep_ctrl_cfg ctrl;   
    struct sstep_callbacks hal;   
};

/* ==============================================================================
 * MEASUREMENT AND STATUS TYPES
 * =============================================================================*/

struct sstep_sample
{
    uint16_t i_a;  
    uint16_t i_b;  
    uint16_t vbus; 
};

struct sstep_status
{
    enum sstep_state state;  
    uint16_t faults;         
    int32_t position;        
    int32_t target;          
    int32_t velocity;        
    int32_t i_a_ma;          
    int32_t i_b_ma;          
    uint32_t vbus_mv;        
    int32_t emf_d_mv;        
    int32_t emf_q_mv;        
    int32_t rotor_velocity;  
    int32_t load_angle_cdeg; 
    uint8_t stall_level_pct; 
};

/* ==============================================================================
 * DRIVER INSTANCE
 * =============================================================================*/

#if defined(UINTPTR_MAX) && (UINTPTR_MAX > 0xFFFFFFFFU)
#define SSTEP_CONFIG_BYTES 176U
#if (SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND == SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FIXED)
#define SSTEP_STATE_BYTES 288U
#else
#define SSTEP_STATE_BYTES 312U
#endif
#else
#define SSTEP_CONFIG_BYTES 152U
#if (SSTEP_CFG_MATH_BACKEND == SSTEP_MATH_BACKEND_FIXED)
#define SSTEP_STATE_BYTES 280U
#else
#define SSTEP_STATE_BYTES 304U
#endif
#endif

#define SSTEP_INSTANCE_WORDS ((SSTEP_CONFIG_BYTES + SSTEP_STATE_BYTES + 7U) / 8U)

struct sstep
{
    uint64_t opaque[SSTEP_INSTANCE_WORDS]; 
};

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* SSTEP_CTRL_H */

#define SSTEP_FAULT_STALL 0x0020U

/* ==============================================================================

 * =============================================================================*/

enum sstep_state
{
    SSTEP_STATE_DISABLED = 0, 
    SSTEP_STATE_HOLDING = 1,  
    SSTEP_STATE_MOVING = 2,

docs.text:
Map requested phase voltages to leg compare values (averaged power stage). 

void sstep_bridge_map (
    enum sstep_topology topology,
    sstep_acc_t va,
    sstep_acc_t vb,
    const struct sstep_gain * inv_vbus,
    sstep_acc_t vbus,
    uint16_t period,
    struct sstep_bridge_out * out
)

The voltage vector is scaled down with its direction kept when the stage cannot produce it: full bridge |a|, |b| <= 1, shared leg max(a,b,0) - min(a,b,0) <= 1, a and b relative to the measured bus voltage. Shared leg: common leg centred.

Parameters:

  • topology Power stage topology (compiled in).
  • va Requested phase voltages [pu of V_base].
  • inv_vbus V_base / bus voltage.
  • vbus Bus voltage [pu of V_base], 0 .. 2.
  • period Compare value for 100 % duty cycle.
  • out Result.

/*******************************************************************************
 * Stepper-C: Stepper Motor Control Implementation
 *
 * Project:     Stepper-C - Hardware-Agnostic Stepper Motor Control Library
 * Description: Averaged power stage: phase voltage request to leg compare values, both topologies.
 *
 * Author:      Anton Vynohradov

 ******************************************************************************/


/* ==============================================================================
 * INCLUDES
 * =============================================================================*/

#include "sstep_internal.h"

/* ==============================================================================
 * DEFINES & MACROS
 * =============================================================================*/

#define ACC_HALF SSTEP_ACC_HALF

/* ==============================================================================
 * PRIVATE FUNCTION DECLARATIONS
 * =============================================================================*/

static sstep_acc_t acc_max(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b);
#if (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG == 1)
static sstep_acc_t acc_min(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b);
#endif
static sstep_acc_t scale_to_unit(sstep_acc_t x, sstep_acc_t m);
#if (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE == 1)
static sstep_acc_t span_full(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b);
static void duties_full(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b, uint16_t period,
                        struct sstep_bridge_out* out);
#endif
#if (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG == 1)
static sstep_acc_t span_shared(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b);
static void duties_shared(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b, uint16_t period,
                          struct sstep_bridge_out* out);
#endif

/* ==============================================================================
 * PRIVATE FUNCTION IMPLEMENTATIONS
 * =============================================================================*/

static sstep_acc_t acc_max(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b)
{
    return (a > b) ? a : b;
}

#if (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG == 1)
static sstep_acc_t acc_min(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b)
{
    return (a < b) ? a : b;
}
#endif

static sstep_acc_t scale_to_unit(sstep_acc_t x, sstep_acc_t m)
{
    sstep_acc_t q = sstep_acc_from_real(sstep_div_unit(sstep_acc_abs(x), m));
    return (x < SSTEP_ACC_ZERO) ? -q : q;
}

#if (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE == 1)

static sstep_acc_t span_full(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b)
{
    return acc_max(sstep_acc_abs(a), sstep_acc_abs(b));
}

static void duties_full(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b, uint16_t period, struct sstep_bridge_out* out)
{
    sstep_acc_t ha = sstep_acc_halve(a);
    sstep_acc_t hb = sstep_acc_halve(b);
    out->compare[0] = sstep_acc_to_ticks(ACC_HALF + ha, period);
    out->compare[1] = sstep_acc_to_ticks(ACC_HALF - ha, period);
    out->compare[2] = sstep_acc_to_ticks(ACC_HALF + hb, period);
    out->compare[3] = sstep_acc_to_ticks(ACC_HALF - hb, period);
}

#endif

#if (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG == 1)

static sstep_acc_t span_shared(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b)
{
    return acc_max(acc_max(a, b), SSTEP_ACC_ZERO) - acc_min(acc_min(a, b), SSTEP_ACC_ZERO);
}

static void duties_shared(sstep_acc_t a, sstep_acc_t b, uint16_t period,
                          struct sstep_bridge_out* out)
{
    sstep_acc_t hi = acc_max(acc_max(a, b), SSTEP_ACC_ZERO);
    sstep_acc_t lo = acc_min(acc_min(a, b), SSTEP_ACC_ZERO);
    sstep_acc_t w = ACC_HALF - sstep_acc_halve(hi + lo);
    out->compare[0] = sstep_acc_to_ticks(a + w, period);
    out->compare[1] = sstep_acc_to_ticks(b + w, period);
    out->compare[2] = sstep_acc_to_ticks(w, period);
    out->compare[3] = 0U;
}

#endif

/* ==============================================================================
 * PUBLIC FUNCTION IMPLEMENTATIONS (library internal)
 * =============================================================================*/

void sstep_bridge_map(enum sstep_topology topology, sstep_acc_t va, sstep_acc_t vb,
                      const struct sstep_gain* inv_vbus, sstep_acc_t vbus, uint16_t period,
                      struct sstep_bridge_out* out)
{
    sstep_acc_t x = va;
    sstep_acc_t y = vb;
    sstep_acc_t m0 = acc_max(sstep_acc_abs(va), sstep_acc_abs(vb));
    sstep_acc_t a;
    sstep_acc_t b;
    sstep_acc_t m;

    /* Power-of-two pre-scale keeps the direction exactly and the request below 4 pu,
       the input range of the multiplication by V_base / Vbus (Vbus <= 2 pu, so a
       pre-scaled request is always limited below). Bounded: fixed point at most 14
       halvings (2^31 / 2^17); float at most 18 (the PI output is below 2^20 pu). */
    while (m0 > SSTEP_ACC_IN_MAX)
    {
        x = sstep_acc_halve(x);
        y = sstep_acc_halve(y);
        m0 = sstep_acc_halve(m0);
    }

    /* relative to the bus voltage: 1.0 = Vbus */
    a = sstep_gain_mul_acc(inv_vbus, x);
    b = sstep_gain_mul_acc(inv_vbus, y);

#if (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE == 1) && (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG == 1)
    m = (topology == SSTEP_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE) ? span_full(a, b) : span_shared(a, b);
#elif (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE == 1)
    (void)topology;
    m = span_full(a, b);
#else
    (void)topology;
    m = span_shared(a, b);
#endif

    out->limited = (m > SSTEP_ACC_ONE);
    if (out->limited)
    {
        a = scale_to_unit(a, m);
        b = scale_to_unit(b, m);
        /* applied voltage in pu of V_base: a * Vbus */
        out->v[0] = sstep_acc_scale(vbus, sstep_acc_to_real(a));
        out->v[1] = sstep_acc_scale(vbus, sstep_acc_to_real(b));
    }
    else
    {
        out->v[0] = va;
        out->v[1] = vb;
    }

#if (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE == 1) && (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_SHARED_LEG == 1)
    if (topology == SSTEP_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE)
    {
        duties_full(a, b, period, out);
    }
    else
    {
        duties_shared(a, b, period, out);
    }
#elif (SSTEP_CFG_TOPOLOGY_FULL_BRIDGE == 1)
    duties_full(a, b, period, out);
#else
    duties_shared(a, b, period, out);
#endif
}

/*******************************************************************************
 * Stepper-C: Stepper Motor Control Implementation
 *
 * Project:     Stepper-C - Hardware-Agnostic Stepper Motor Control Library
 * Description: Public API: initialisation, fast loop (current control), slow loop (motion), commands.
